173	Except as expressly set forth in this Article 4, Physician shall not receive any other compensation, remuneration, benefit, or thing of value from Employer, or from any entity in which Employer has a financial relationship, in connection with Physician\'s employment or Physician\'s referral of patients for designated health services. Physician acknowledges that the compensation set forth herein has been determined based on fair market value for the services to be provided by Physician and does not take into account the volume or value of any referrals by Physician for designated health services or otherwise.
174	
175	**[ARTICLE 5 --- BILLING AND COLLECTIONS]{.underline}**
176	
177	**Section 5.1 --- Billing**
178	
179	All professional fees for services rendered by Physician during the Term shall be billed by and collected by Employer. Physician hereby assigns to Employer all rights to bill and collect for professional medical services rendered by Physician during the Term. All billings shall be submitted under Employer\'s group National Provider Identifier (NPI) and Tax Identification Number (EIN 31-4527893), in accordance with applicable billing regulations.
180	
181	**Section 5.2 --- Coding and Documentation**
182	
183	Physician shall accurately and completely document all patient encounters and shall code services in compliance with applicable coding guidelines, including Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) and International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10). Physician shall cooperate with Employer\'s billing department and compliance program in all matters related to billing accuracy, claim submission, and regulatory compliance.
184	
185	**[ARTICLE 6 --- COMPLIANCE WITH LAWS]{.underline}**
186	
187	**Section 6.1 --- General Compliance**
188	
189	Physician shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, rules, and regulations governing the practice of medicine and the provision of health care services, including without limitation:
190	
191	> \(a\) the federal physician self-referral law, 42 U.S.C. § 1395nn (the \"Stark Law\"), and its implementing regulations at 42 C.F.R. Part 411, Subpart J;
192	>
193	> \(b\) the federal Anti-Kickback Statute, 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7b(b), and its implementing regulations and safe harbors;
194	>
195	> \(c\) the False Claims Act, 31 U.S.C. §§ 3729--3733;
196	>
197	> \(d\) the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (\"HIPAA\") and all applicable privacy, security, and breach notification regulations; and
198	>
199	> \(e\) the Ohio Revised Code provisions governing the practice of medicine, including Ohio Rev. Code Chapter 4731.
200	
201	**Section 6.2 --- Compliance Program**
202	
203	Physician shall comply with Employer\'s Compliance Program as set forth in the Greenfield Health Partners Compliance Program Manual, adopted April 15, 2021, as may be amended from time to time. Physician shall attend all annual compliance training sessions conducted by Employer and shall promptly report any suspected violations of law, regulation, or Employer policy through the compliance hotline or directly to the Chief Compliance Officer, Patricia Langford.
204	
205	**Section 6.3 --- Stark Law Representations**
206	
207	The parties acknowledge that Physician may refer patients for designated health services (\"DHS\") to entities with which Employer has a financial relationship. The parties intend that this Agreement and the compensation arrangements hereunder comply with the employment exception to the Stark Law set forth at 42 C.F.R. § 411.357(c). Physician\'s compensation under this Agreement:
208	
209	> \(i\) is set at fair market value for the services provided by Physician;
210	>
211	> \(ii\) is not determined in any manner that takes into account the volume or value of Physician\'s referrals for designated health services; and
212	>
213	> \(iii\) is provided pursuant to a written agreement signed by the parties covering the services to be furnished by Physician.
214	
215	The parties shall use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure ongoing compliance with the requirements of the employment exception throughout the Term of this Agreement.
216	
217	**[ARTICLE 7 --- INSURANCE AND INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**
218	
219	**Section 7.1 --- Professional Liability Insurance**
220	
221	Employer shall provide and maintain professional liability (malpractice) insurance for Physician during the Term, with minimum coverage limits of One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000.00) per occurrence and Three Million Dollars (\$3,000,000.00) in the aggregate, on an occurrence basis. In the event such coverage is converted to a claims-made basis, Employer shall provide tail coverage for Physician for a period of not less than three (3) years following the effective date of termination or expiration of this Agreement.
222	
223	**Section 7.2 --- Indemnification**
224	
225	Employer shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Physician from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising from any act or omission of Employer, its agents, or its other employees, except to the extent such claims arise from Physician\'s own professional negligence or willful misconduct. Physician shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Employer from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising from Physician\'s professional negligence or willful misconduct in the performance of his duties under this Agreement.
226	
227	**[ARTICLE 8 --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**
228	
229	**Section 8.1 --- Confidential Information**
230	
231	Physician agrees to maintain the confidentiality of all proprietary and confidential information of Employer, including but not limited to patient lists, referral sources, referral patterns, financial data, compensation structures, fee schedules, business plans, strategic initiatives, and trade secrets. Physician shall not disclose such information to any third party without the prior written consent of Employer. This confidentiality obligation shall survive termination or expiration of this Agreement for a period of three (3) years.
232	
233	**Section 8.2 --- HIPAA Compliance**
234	
235	Physician shall comply with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (\"HIPAA\") and all applicable patient privacy and security regulations in connection with the use and disclosure of protected health information. Physician acknowledges receipt of Employer\'s Notice of Privacy Practices, dated most recently as of March 1, 2021.
236	
237	**[ARTICLE 9 --- RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS]{.underline}**
238	
239	**Section 9.1 --- Non-Competition**
240	
241	During the Term and for a period of one (1) year following the termination or expiration of this Agreement for any reason, Physician shall not directly or indirectly engage in the practice of Internal Medicine, whether as an employee, independent contractor, partner, owner, or otherwise, within a fifteen (15) mile radius of any Greenfield Health Partners practice location at which Physician provided services during the twelve (12) months preceding the date of termination or expiration. Physician acknowledges that Employer currently operates twelve (12) locations across the Columbus, Ohio metropolitan area.
242	
243	**Section 9.2 --- Non-Solicitation**
244	
245	For a period of two (2) years following the termination or expiration of this Agreement for any reason, Physician shall not, directly or indirectly:
246	
247	> \(a\) solicit, contact, or treat any patient of Employer whom Physician treated or for whom Physician provided medical services during the twenty-four (24) months preceding the date of termination or expiration; or
248	>
249	> \(b\) solicit, recruit, hire, or encourage the departure of any employee, physician, or contractor of Employer.
250	
251	**Section 9.3 --- Remedies**
252	
253	Physician acknowledges that a breach of the restrictive covenants set forth in this Article 9 would cause Employer irreparable harm for which monetary damages would be an inadequate remedy. Accordingly, Employer shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief, including temporary restraining orders and preliminary and permanent injunctions, in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity, without the necessity of posting bond.
254	
255	**[ARTICLE 10 --- DISPUTE RESOLUTION]{.underline}**
256	
257	**Section 10.1 --- Mediation**
258	
259	Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach, termination, or validity thereof, shall first be submitted to non-binding mediation in Columbus, Ohio, administered by a mediator mutually agreed upon by the parties, before either party may initiate arbitration proceedings.
260	
261	**Section 10.2 --- Arbitration**
262	
263	If mediation is unsuccessful within sixty (60) days of the initiation of mediation proceedings, the dispute shall be resolved by final and binding arbitration in Columbus, Ohio, in accordance with the Commercial Arbitration Rules of the American Arbitration Association then in effect. The arbitrator shall be selected in accordance with such rules and shall have experience in health care law. The decision and award of the arbitrator shall be final and binding, and judgment upon the award may be entered in any court of competent jurisdiction. Each party shall bear its own costs and attorneys\' fees, except as the arbitrator may otherwise determine.
264	
265	**[ARTICLE 11 --- GENERAL PROVISIONS]{.underline}**
266	
267	**Section 11.1 --- Entire Agreement**
268	
269	This Agreement, together with any written amendments hereto executed by both parties, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior oral or written agreements, understandings, representations, or negotiations between the parties relating to the subject matter hereof. No modification, amendment, or waiver of any provision of this Agreement shall be effective unless in writing and signed by both parties.
270	
271	**Section 11.2 --- Assignment**
272	
273	This Agreement is personal to Physician and shall not be assigned or delegated by Physician. Employer may assign this Agreement to any successor entity, whether by merger, consolidation, sale of assets, or otherwise, upon written notice to Physician, provided that the successor entity assumes all obligations of Employer hereunder.
274	
275	**Section 11.3 --- Notices**
276	
277	All notices, requests, demands, or other communications required or permitted under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed duly given when delivered personally, or when sent by certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid, or by nationally recognized overnight courier, addressed as follows:
278	
279	> **If to Employer:** Greenfield Health Partners, LLC
280	>
281	> Attn: Managing Member
282	>
283	> 2800 Riverside Medical Plaza, Suite 400 Columbus, OH 43215
284	>
285	> **If to Physician:** Dr. Thomas Wellford, M.D. At the address on file with Employer\'s Human Resources Department
286	
287	Either party may change its address for notices by providing written notice to the other party in accordance with this Section.
288	
289	**Section 11.4 --- Governing Law**
290	
291	This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Ohio, without giving effect to principles of conflicts of law. To the extent this Agreement involves services payable by federal health care programs, the parties acknowledge that federal law, including 42 U.S.C. § 1395nn and 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7b, shall apply and shall preempt any inconsistent state law provisions.
292	
293	**Section 11.5 --- Severability**
294	
295	If any provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable by a court or tribunal of competent jurisdiction, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect. If any provision is deemed to violate applicable law, including the Stark Law or the Anti-Kickback Statute, the parties shall negotiate in good faith to reform such provision to achieve the parties\' original intent in a lawful manner, consistent with applicable regulatory requirements.
296	
297	**Section 11.6 --- Waiver**
298	
299	The failure of either party to enforce any provision of this Agreement shall not constitute a waiver of such provision or the right to enforce it at a later time. No waiver of any breach shall be deemed a waiver of any subsequent breach.
300	
301	**Section 11.7 --- Counterparts**
302	
303	This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument.
304	
305	**IN WITNESS WHEREOF**, the parties have executed this Employment Agreement as of the Effective Date first written above.
306	
307	**GREENFIELD HEALTH PARTNERS, LLC**
308

**MEDICAL DIRECTOR AGREEMENT**

Between

**Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC**

and

**Raymond K. Stein, M.D.**

Effective as of August 22, 2016

This Medical Director Agreement (this \"**Agreement**\") is entered into as of August 22, 2016 (the \"**Effective Date**\"), by and between **Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC**, an Ohio limited liability company formed on August 22, 2016, with its principal place of business at 2850 Riverside Medical Plaza, Suite 100, Columbus, OH 43215 (the \"**Center**\" or \"**ASC**\"), and **Raymond K. Stein, M.D.**, an individual residing in the State of Ohio, board certified in Orthopedic Surgery (the \"**Medical Director**\" or \"**Physician**,\" and together with the Center, the \"**Parties**,\" and each individually, a \"**Party**\").

The Center desires to engage Dr. Stein as Medical Director to provide medical oversight, quality assurance, and administrative services to the Center in connection with its ambulatory surgical operations, and Dr. Stein desires to accept such engagement, on the terms and conditions set forth herein.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements hereinafter set forth, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS**, the Center is a Medicare-certified ambulatory surgical center providing outpatient surgical services in Columbus, Ohio;

**WHEREAS**, the Center is owned by Greenfield Health Partners, LLC (sixty percent (60%)), Dr. Raymond K. Stein, M.D. (twenty-five percent (25%)), and Dr. Priya Narayan, M.D. (fifteen percent (15%));

**WHEREAS**, the Center requires the services of a qualified physician to serve as Medical Director to oversee clinical operations, quality assurance, and regulatory compliance in accordance with applicable Medicare Conditions for Coverage and state licensure requirements;

**WHEREAS**, Dr. Stein is a physician duly licensed to practice medicine in the State of Ohio, board certified in Orthopedic Surgery by the American Board of Orthopaedic Surgery, and serves as Managing Member and Chief Medical Officer of Greenfield Health Partners, LLC, an Ohio limited liability company with its principal office at 2800 Riverside Medical Plaza, Suite 400, Columbus, OH 43215;

**WHEREAS**, the Parties represent that the compensation set forth herein reflects fair market value for the Medical Director services to be rendered and has been determined without regard to the volume or value of any referrals or other business generated between the Parties; and

**WHEREAS**, the Parties intend this Agreement to comply with all applicable federal and state laws, including without limitation the Ethics in Patient Referrals Act (42 U.S.C. § 1395nn), the federal Anti-Kickback Statute (42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7b(b)), and applicable provisions of the Ohio Revised Code.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the foregoing Recitals, which are incorporated herein by reference, and the mutual promises and covenants contained herein, the Parties agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below:

**\"Center\"** means Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC, an Ohio limited liability company.

**\"Compensation Committee\" means the compensation committee of Greenfield Health Partners, LLC, currently consisting of Dr. Raymond K. Stein, M.D. (Chair), Dr. Priya Narayan, M.D., and Alan Cromdale Consulting, CFO.**

**\"Greenfield\"** means Greenfield Health Partners, LLC, an Ohio limited liability company, EIN 31-4527893.

**\"Medical Director Services\"** means the services described in Article III of this Agreement.

**\"Term\"** means the Initial Term and any Renewal Term, as defined in Article II of this Agreement.

**[ARTICLE II --- TERM AND RENEWAL]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1 --- Initial Term.** The initial term of this Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue for a period of one (1) year, expiring on August 21, 2017, unless earlier terminated in accordance with Article VII (the \"**Initial Term**\").

**Section 2.2 --- Automatic Renewal.** Upon expiration of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive one (1)-year periods (each a \"**Renewal Term**\") on the same terms and conditions set forth herein, unless either Party provides written notice of non-renewal to the other Party at least sixty (60) days prior to the expiration of the then-current Initial Term or Renewal Term, as applicable. For purposes of this Agreement, the Initial Term and any Renewal Term(s) shall be collectively referred to as the \"**Term**.\"

**Section 2.3 --- Terms Upon Renewal.** Each Renewal Term shall be on the same terms and conditions as set forth in this Agreement as of the Effective Date. No additional action, approval, or documentation shall be required to effectuate any Renewal Term.

**[ARTICLE III --- MEDICAL DIRECTOR SERVICES AND DUTIES]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- Scope of Services.** Medical Director shall provide the following services to the Center during the Term (collectively, the \"**Medical Director Services**\"):

> \(a\) Oversee and supervise clinical quality assurance and improvement programs;
>
> \(b\) Develop, review, and approve clinical protocols, policies, and procedures for surgical services performed at the Center;
>
> \(c\) Participate in credentialing and privileging of physicians and allied health professionals at the Center;
>
> \(d\) Review adverse events, complications, and patient safety incidents and recommend corrective actions;
>
> \(e\) Attend and chair the Center\'s Medical Advisory Committee meetings, which shall be held no less frequently than quarterly;
>
> \(f\) Serve as liaison between the Center\'s administration and medical staff;
>
> \(g\) Ensure compliance with applicable state and federal regulations, including Medicare Conditions for Coverage for Ambulatory Surgical Centers (42 C.F.R. Part 416);
>
> \(h\) Review and approve infection control protocols and related policies;
>
> \(i\) Provide consultation to Center staff on clinical matters as reasonably requested; and
>
> \(j\) Such other duties as may be reasonably assigned by the Center\'s governing body from time to time, consistent with Medical Director\'s qualifications and the scope of this Agreement.

**Section 3.2 --- Time Commitment.** Medical Director shall devote a minimum of eight (8) hours per month to the performance of Medical Director Services, which time commitment equates to approximately ninety-six (96) hours per year. The Parties acknowledge that this time commitment represents the anticipated average, and actual hours may vary from month to month depending on the operational needs of the Center. Medical Director shall maintain contemporaneous time records documenting the hours devoted to Medical Director Services and shall make such records available to the Center upon reasonable request.

**Section 3.3 --- Location of Services.** Medical Director Services shall be performed primarily at the Center\'s facility located at 2850 Riverside Medical Plaza, Suite 100, Columbus, OH 43215, or at such other locations as may be reasonably required for the performance of such services, including by telephone or electronic communication.

**Section 3.4 --- Standard of Care.** Medical Director shall perform all Medical Director Services hereunder in a professional manner consistent with prevailing standards of medical practice, applicable accreditation standards, and all applicable laws and regulations.

**[ARTICLE IV --- COMPENSATION]{.underline}**

**Section 4.1 --- Annual Compensation.** In consideration of the Medical Director Services to be rendered hereunder, the Center shall pay Medical Director an annual fee of One Hundred Twenty Thousand Dollars (\$120,000.00) (the \"**Annual Compensation**\"), payable in equal monthly installments of Ten Thousand Dollars (\$10,000.00), due on the last business day of each calendar month during the Term. Payment shall be made by check or electronic funds transfer to an account designated in writing by Medical Director.

**Section 4.2 --- Fair Market Value Representation.** The Parties represent and warrant that the Annual Compensation set forth in Section 4.1 reflects fair market value for the Medical Director Services described in Article III, taking into account the time commitment set forth in Section 3.2, Medical Director\'s qualifications, training, and experience, and the nature and scope of the services to be performed. The Parties further represent that the Annual Compensation has been determined without regard to the volume or value of referrals or other business generated between the Parties or their respective affiliates.

**Section 4.3 --- No Additional Compensation.** Medical Director shall not be entitled to any additional compensation, bonuses, incentive payments, or other remuneration from the Center for Medical Director Services beyond the Annual Compensation set forth in Section 4.1. For the avoidance of doubt, this Section 4.3 does not affect any compensation, profit distributions, or other payments Medical Director may receive in his capacity as an owner (member) of the Center, which shall be governed exclusively by the Center\'s Operating Agreement, as amended from time to time.

**Section 4.4 --- Expenses.** The Center shall reimburse Medical Director for reasonable, documented out-of-pocket expenses incurred in connection with the performance of Medical Director Services, provided that such expenses are pre-approved by the Center\'s administrator and supported by appropriate documentation. Reimbursement shall be made within thirty (30) days of submission of a proper expense report.

**[ARTICLE V --- RELATIONSHIP OF THE PARTIES]{.underline}**

**Section 5.1 --- Independent Contractor Status.** Medical Director shall perform all services under this Agreement as an independent contractor and not as an employee, agent, partner, or joint venturer of the Center. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to create a partnership, joint venture, or agency relationship between the Parties, except as expressly set forth herein. Medical Director shall have no authority to bind the Center or to incur any obligation on behalf of the Center except as expressly authorized in writing by the Center\'s governing body.

**Section 5.2 --- Tax Obligations.** Medical Director shall be solely responsible for all federal, state, and local income taxes, self-employment taxes, and other taxes arising from compensation received under this Agreement. The Center shall not withhold any taxes from payments made to Medical Director hereunder and shall issue an IRS Form 1099-NEC (or successor form) to Medical Director for all compensation paid under this Agreement in each calendar year.

**Section 5.3 --- Other Activities.** Nothing in this Agreement shall prohibit Medical Director from engaging in other professional activities, including but not limited to the practice of medicine, consulting, teaching, or other business endeavors, provided such activities do not materially interfere with Medical Director\'s obligations under this Agreement. The Parties acknowledge that Medical Director serves as Managing Member and Chief Medical Officer of Greenfield Health Partners, LLC, and maintains an active orthopedic surgery practice.

**[ARTICLE VI --- CONFIDENTIALITY AND COMPLIANCE]{.underline}**

**Section 6.1 --- Confidentiality.** Medical Director shall maintain the confidentiality of all proprietary and confidential information of the Center, including but not limited to patient information, financial data, business plans, operational information, trade secrets, and strategic plans. Medical Director shall not disclose such information to any third party without the prior written consent of the Center, except as required by law. This obligation shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement.

**Section 6.2 --- HIPAA Compliance.** Medical Director shall comply with all applicable provisions of the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (\"HIPAA\"), as amended by the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act (\"HITECH Act\"), and their implementing regulations, including the Standards for Privacy of Individually Identifiable Health Information (45 C.F.R. Parts 160 and 164). The Center and Medical Director shall execute a separate Business Associate Agreement if required under applicable HIPAA regulations.

**Section 6.3 --- Regulatory Compliance.** The Parties intend that this Agreement comply with all applicable federal and state laws and regulations, including without limitation:

> \(a\) The Ethics in Patient Referrals Act, 42 U.S.C. § 1395nn (the \"**Stark Law**\"), and its implementing regulations at 42 C.F.R. § 411.350 *et seq.*;
>
> \(b\) The Federal Anti-Kickback Statute, 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7b(b), and its implementing safe harbor regulations at 42 C.F.R. § 1001.952; and
>
> \(c\) Ohio Revised Code provisions governing physician self-referral, fee-splitting, and related matters.

**Section 6.4 --- Compliance Representations.** Each Party represents and warrants that, as of the Effective Date: (a) it has not been excluded from participation in any federal or state health care program, including Medicare and Medicaid; (b) it has not been convicted of any offense related to the delivery of health care services or items; and (c) it is not subject to any pending or threatened investigation, proceeding, or action that could result in such exclusion or conviction. Each Party shall promptly notify the other Party in writing if any of the foregoing representations ceases to be true during the Term.

**Section 6.5 --- Access to Records.** Medical Director shall make available to the Secretary of the United States Department of Health and Human Services, the Comptroller General of the United States, and their authorized representatives, upon request, this Agreement and all books, documents, and records necessary to certify the nature and extent of costs of services provided under this Agreement, in accordance with 42 U.S.C. § 1395x(v)(1)(I) and 42 C.F.R. § 420.300 *et seq.* This obligation shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement for a period of four (4) years.

**[ARTICLE VII --- TERMINATION]{.underline}**

**Section 7.1 --- Termination for Cause.** Either Party may terminate this Agreement immediately upon written notice to the other Party if the other Party:

> \(a\) Materially breaches any provision of this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days after receipt of written notice specifying the nature of the breach;
>
> \(b\) Loses any license, certification, or accreditation required to perform its obligations hereunder;
>
> \(c\) Becomes excluded from participation in any federal health care program, including Medicare or Medicaid;
>
> \(d\) Is convicted of a felony or any crime involving moral turpitude; or
>
> \(e\) In the case of Medical Director, becomes subject to an action by the State Medical Board of Ohio resulting in the suspension or revocation of Medical Director\'s license to practice medicine in the State of Ohio.

**Section 7.2 --- Termination Without Cause.** Either Party may terminate this Agreement without cause upon ninety (90) days\' prior written notice to the other Party, delivered in accordance with Section 8.5.

**Section 7.3 --- Effect of Termination.** Upon the effective date of termination or expiration of this Agreement, the Center shall pay Medical Director for all Medical Director Services rendered through the effective date of termination, prorated on a daily basis for any partial month. The provisions of Section 6.1 (Confidentiality), Section 6.5 (Access to Records), Section 8.4 (Indemnification), and Section 8.7 (Governing Law) shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement.

**Section 7.4 --- No Termination Penalty Related to Referrals.** The termination, expiration, or non-renewal of this Agreement shall not be conditioned upon, or related in any manner to, the volume or value of referrals or other business generated between the Parties or their respective affiliates, including Greenfield Health Partners, LLC.

**[ARTICLE VIII --- GENERAL PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 8.1 --- Entire Agreement.** This Agreement, including the Exhibits attached hereto, constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous negotiations, representations, warranties, understandings, and agreements, whether written or oral, relating to such subject matter.

**Section 8.2 --- Amendments.** This Agreement may not be amended, modified, or supplemented except by a written instrument signed by both Parties.

**Section 8.3 --- Assignment.** This Agreement may not be assigned by either Party without the prior written consent of the other Party, and any attempted assignment without such consent shall be null and void; *provided, however*, that the Center may assign this Agreement to any successor entity in connection with a merger, consolidation, or sale of substantially all of the Center\'s assets without the consent of Medical Director.

**Section 8.4 --- Indemnification.** Each Party (the \"**Indemnifying Party**\") shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other Party and its respective officers, directors, members, managers, employees, and agents (collectively, the \"**Indemnified Parties**\") from and against any and all claims, losses, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and court costs) arising out of or relating to: (a) any breach of this Agreement by the Indemnifying Party; or (b) any negligent or wrongful act or omission of the Indemnifying Party in connection with this Agreement.

**Section 8.5 --- Notices.** All notices, demands, requests, consents, and other communications required or permitted under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed duly given when: (a) delivered personally; (b) sent by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid; or (c) sent by nationally recognized overnight courier, in each case addressed as follows:

> If to the Center:
>
> Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC 2850 Riverside Medical Plaza, Suite 100 Columbus, OH 43215
>
> Attn: Administrator
>
> If to Medical Director:
>
> Raymond K. Stein, M.D. c/o Greenfield Health Partners, LLC 2800 Riverside Medical Plaza, Suite 400 Columbus, OH 43215

Either Party may change its notice address by providing written notice to the other Party in accordance with this Section.

**Section 8.6 --- Severability.** If any provision of this Agreement, or the application thereof to any person or circumstance, is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable in any respect, the validity, legality, and enforceability of the remaining provisions shall not in any way be affected or impaired thereby, and such invalid, illegal, or unenforceable provision shall be modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it valid, legal, and enforceable.

**Section 8.7 --- Governing Law.** This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Ohio, without regard to its conflicts of law principles.

**Section 8.8 --- Counterparts.** This Agreement may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument.

**Section 8.9 --- Waiver.** No failure or delay by either Party in exercising any right, power, or remedy under this Agreement shall operate as a waiver thereof, nor shall any single or partial exercise of any such right, power, or remedy preclude any other or further exercise thereof or the exercise of any other right, power, or remedy. No waiver of any provision of this Agreement shall constitute a waiver of any other provision or of the same provision on any future occasion.

**Section 8.10 --- No Third-Party Beneficiaries.** This Agreement is for the sole benefit of the Parties hereto and their respective permitted successors and assigns, and nothing in this Agreement, express or implied, is intended to or shall confer upon any other person or entity any legal or equitable right, benefit, or remedy of any nature whatsoever under or by reason of this Agreement.

**IN WITNESS WHEREOF**, the Parties have executed this Medical Director Agreement as of the Effective Date first written above.

**BUCKEYE SURGICAL CENTER, LLC**

By: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**

Name: Priya Narayan, M.D.

Title: Member

Date: August 22, 2016

**MEDICAL DIRECTOR**

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

Raymond K. Stein, M.D.

Date: August 22, 2016

**EXHIBIT A**

**DESCRIPTION OF MEDICAL DIRECTOR SERVICES**

The following is a description of the Medical Director Services to be performed by Medical Director pursuant to Article III of this Agreement, together with the estimated time commitment associated with each category of service:

> • **Medical Advisory Committee Meetings:** Attendance at and chairing of quarterly Medical Advisory Committee meetings (four (4) meetings per year, approximately two (2) hours each meeting; estimated total: eight (8) hours per year)
>
> • **Quality Metrics and Outcomes Review:** Monthly review of clinical quality metrics, patient outcomes data, and performance indicators (approximately two (2) hours per month; estimated total: twenty-four (24) hours per year)
>
> • **Policy and Procedure Review:** Annual review and update of clinical policies, procedures, and surgical protocols (approximately eight (8) hours per year)
>
> • **Credentialing and Privileging:** Review of credentialing files and privilege requests for new and existing physician applicants and allied health professionals (as needed)
>
> • **Infection Control and Safety:** Participation in infection control reviews, safety assessments, and related compliance activities (as needed)
>
> • **Clinical Consultation:** Ad hoc clinical consultation with Center staff and administration on matters relating to patient care, clinical operations, and regulatory compliance (as needed)

**Total Estimated Time Commitment:** Approximately eight (8) hours per month / ninety-six (96) hours per year.

**AMENDED AND RESTATED OPERATING AGREEMENT**

**OF**

**BUCKEYE SURGICAL CENTER, LLC**

an Ohio Limited Liability Company

Effective as of August 22, 2016

The following constitutes selected excerpts from the Operating Agreement. Sections not reproduced herein are indicated by bracketed notations.

This Amended and Restated Operating Agreement (this \"**Agreement**\") of Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC, an Ohio limited liability company (the \"**Center**\"), is entered into and effective as of August 22, 2016, by and among the following Members:

> **Greenfield Health Partners, LLC**, an Ohio limited liability company (\"**Greenfield**\"), holding a sixty percent (60%) Membership Interest;
>
> **Dr. Raymond K. Stein, M.D.**, an individual residing in the State of Ohio (\"**Dr. Stein**\"), holding a twenty-five percent (25%) Membership Interest; and
>
> **Dr. Priya Narayan, M.D.**, an individual residing in the State of Ohio (\"**Dr. Narayan**\"), holding a fifteen percent (15%) Membership Interest.

The foregoing parties are referred to individually as a \"**Member**\" and collectively as the \"**Members**.\"

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Members agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

\[Sections 1.1 through 1.8 omitted.\]

**Section 1.9** --- \"**Adjusted Quarterly Referral Volume**\" means, with respect to each Member, the total number of surgical cases referred by such Member (or, in the case of Greenfield Health Partners, LLC, by the physicians of Greenfield Health Partners, LLC) to the Center during the applicable calendar quarter, as determined by the Manager based on Center scheduling and admissions records.

**Section 1.10** --- \"**Center**\" means Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC, an Ohio limited liability company.

**Section 1.11** --- \"**Distributable Cash**\" means net cash receipts of the Center for the applicable period, less reserves for operating expenses, capital expenditures, and contingencies as determined by the Manager in accordance with this Agreement.

**Section 1.12** --- \"**Facility Fee Revenue**\" means gross revenue received by the Center for facility fees billed in connection with surgical cases performed at the Center.

**Section 1.13** --- \"**Manager**\" means Greenfield Health Partners, LLC, or such other Member as may be designated pursuant to Section 5.1.

**Section 1.14** --- \"**Medical Director**\" means the individual appointed pursuant to Section 5.4 to serve as the medical director of the Center.

\[Sections 1.15 through 1.32 omitted, except as set forth below.\]

**Section 1.18** --- \"**Medical Director Agreement**\" means that certain Medical Director Services Agreement dated as of August 22, 2016, by and between the Center and Dr. Raymond K. Stein, M.D., as the same may be amended, restated, or supplemented from time to time.

**Section 1.20** --- \"**Member**\" means each of Greenfield Health Partners, LLC, Dr. Raymond K. Stein, M.D., and Dr. Priya Narayan, M.D., and any person admitted as a member of the Center pursuant to Article IX.

**Section 1.21** --- \"**Membership Interest**\" means a Member\'s percentage ownership interest in the Center as set forth in Section 3.1 and on Exhibit A attached hereto.

**Section 1.23** --- \"**Net Profits**\" and \"**Net Losses**\" mean the net income or net loss of the Center for the applicable period as determined in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles consistently applied, as adjusted by the Center\'s independent accountant.

**Section 1.25** --- \"**Qualified Surgical Case Referral**\" means a surgical case referred to the Center by a Member or, in the case of Greenfield Health Partners, LLC, by a physician who is a member, employee, or contractor of Greenfield Health Partners, LLC, where (a) the patient is scheduled for and undergoes a surgical procedure at the Center, and (b) the referring physician is identified in the Center\'s scheduling system as the referring or ordering physician.

**Section 1.26** --- \"**Referral Percentage**\" means, with respect to each Member, the ratio of such Member\'s Adjusted Quarterly Referral Volume to the total Adjusted Quarterly Referral Volume of all Members for the applicable calendar quarter, expressed as a percentage.

**[ARTICLE II --- FORMATION AND PURPOSE]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1 --- Formation.** The Center was formed as an Ohio limited liability company on August 22, 2016, by the filing of Articles of Organization with the Ohio Secretary of State pursuant to the Ohio Revised Code, Chapter 1706.

**Section 2.2 --- Principal Office.** The principal office of the Center shall be located at 2850 Riverside Medical Plaza, Suite 100, Columbus, OH 43215, or at such other location as the Manager may determine from time to time.

**Section 2.3 --- Purpose.** The purpose of the Center is to own, operate, and manage an ambulatory surgical center and to engage in any and all lawful activities related thereto.

\[Remainder of Article II omitted.\]

**[ARTICLE III --- MEMBERS; CAPITAL CONTRIBUTIONS; MEMBERSHIP INTERESTS]{.underline}**

**[Section 3.1 --- Members and Membership Interests]{.underline}**

The Members and their respective Membership Interests are as follows:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Member**                          **Membership Interest**
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
  Greenfield Health Partners, LLC     60%

  Dr. Raymond K. Stein, M.D.          25%

  Dr. Priya Narayan, M.D.             15%
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

The Membership Interests set forth above are subject to adjustment only pursuant to Article IX (Transfers and Admissions) of this Agreement. A complete schedule of Members, including addresses and initial capital contributions, is attached hereto as **Exhibit A** and incorporated herein by reference. For purposes of this Agreement, Dr. Stein is identified as the Managing Member and Chief Medical Officer of Greenfield Health Partners, LLC, and Dr. Narayan is identified as a member physician (Cardiology) of Greenfield Health Partners, LLC. Each of Dr. Stein and Dr. Narayan enters into this Agreement both in his or her individual capacity as a Member and as a physician affiliated with Greenfield Health Partners, LLC.

**[Section 3.2 --- Initial Capital Contributions]{.underline}**

Each Member made an initial capital contribution to the Center at the time of formation in the amounts set forth on Exhibit A. \[Details of initial capital contributions omitted.\]

**[Section 3.3 --- Additional Capital Contributions]{.underline}**

\[Section 3.3 omitted.\]

**[ARTICLE IV --- ALLOCATIONS AND DISTRIBUTIONS]{.underline}**

**[Section 4.1 --- Allocation of Net Profits and Net Losses]{.underline}**

**(a)** Net Profits and Net Losses of the Center for each fiscal year shall be allocated among the Members in proportion to each Member\'s Referral Percentage for such fiscal year, as determined by averaging the Referral Percentages for the four calendar quarters comprising such fiscal year.

**(b)** For the avoidance of doubt, allocations of Net Profits and Net Losses shall not be made in proportion to Membership Interests but rather shall be made exclusively based on each Member\'s Referral Percentage. The Members acknowledge and agree that this allocation methodology reflects the Members\' agreement that the economic benefits of the Center should be distributed in a manner that reflects each Member\'s contribution to the Center\'s surgical case volume.

**(c)** By way of illustration, if Greenfield Health Partners, LLC refers 702 surgical cases in a fiscal year, Dr. Stein refers 342 cases, and Dr. Narayan refers 56 cases (total: 1,100 cases), Greenfield\'s Referral Percentage would be 63.8%, Dr. Stein\'s Referral Percentage would be 31.1%, and Dr. Narayan\'s Referral Percentage would be 5.1%. Actual allocations shall be calculated based on actual referral data for each fiscal year. The foregoing illustration is hypothetical only and does not reflect actual or projected referral volumes.

**[Section 4.2 --- Quarterly Distributions of Distributable Cash]{.underline}**

**(a)** Subject to Section 4.4, Distributable Cash shall be distributed to the Members on a quarterly basis, within forty-five (45) days following the end of each calendar quarter, in proportion to each Member\'s Referral Percentage for such quarter.

**(b)** The Manager shall determine each Member\'s Adjusted Quarterly Referral Volume based on the Center\'s scheduling and admissions records, and shall provide each Member with a written statement setting forth the calculation of such Member\'s Referral Percentage for the applicable quarter no later than thirty (30) days following the end of each calendar quarter.

**(c)** Distributions shall be made by wire transfer or check to the account or address designated by each Member in writing to the Manager.

**[Section 4.3 --- Tax Distributions]{.underline}**

Notwithstanding any other provision of this Article IV, the Center shall distribute to each Member, on or before each estimated tax payment date, an amount sufficient to enable such Member to satisfy its estimated federal and state income tax obligations arising from such Member\'s allocable share of the Center\'s taxable income. \[Detailed tax distribution calculation methodology omitted.\]

**[Section 4.4 --- Reserves]{.underline}**

The Manager may, in its reasonable discretion, establish reserves from Distributable Cash for working capital, capital expenditures, debt service, and other purposes as the Manager deems appropriate. Any amounts retained as reserves shall be distributed to Members when the Manager determines such reserves are no longer necessary, in proportion to each Member\'s Referral Percentage for the quarter in which such distribution is made.

**[Section 4.5 --- Greenfield Internal Allocation; Referral Credits]{.underline}**

**(a)** Greenfield Health Partners, LLC acknowledges and agrees that it shall, pursuant to its own operating agreement or internal policies, allocate and distribute its share of distributions received from the Center among the individual physicians of Greenfield Health Partners, LLC who referred surgical cases to the Center during the applicable period. Without limiting the foregoing, Greenfield Health Partners, LLC has represented to the other Members that its internal allocation methodology includes a \"referral credit\" mechanism pursuant to which each Greenfield physician who refers a Qualified Surgical Case Referral to the Center shall receive a credit equal to zero point five percent (0.5%) of the Facility Fee Revenue generated by such referred case, which credit shall be added to such physician\'s annual profit distribution from Greenfield Health Partners, LLC.

**(b)** The Members acknowledge that such internal allocation methodology is determined solely by Greenfield Health Partners, LLC and that neither Dr. Stein nor Dr. Narayan, in their capacity as Members of the Center, shall have any obligation or liability with respect to the internal allocation decisions of Greenfield Health Partners, LLC.

**(c)** Greenfield Health Partners, LLC shall maintain records of its internal allocation of Center distributions and shall make such records available to the other Members upon reasonable request.

**[ARTICLE V --- MANAGEMENT]{.underline}**

**[Section 5.1 --- Manager]{.underline}**

Greenfield Health Partners, LLC shall serve as the Manager of the Center and shall have full authority to manage the day-to-day business and affairs of the Center, subject to the provisions of this Agreement.

\[Sections 5.2 and 5.3 omitted --- relating to Manager authority and Member voting rights.\]

**[Section 5.4 --- Medical Director]{.underline}**

**(a)** The Center shall retain a Medical Director pursuant to the Medical Director Agreement. The initial Medical Director shall be Dr. Raymond K. Stein, M.D.

**(b)** The Medical Director shall be responsible for: (i) overseeing the clinical quality and safety of surgical services provided at the Center; (ii) establishing and maintaining clinical protocols, policies, and procedures; (iii) credentialing and peer review of physicians performing procedures at the Center; (iv) serving as liaison between the Center and applicable state and federal regulatory bodies regarding clinical matters; and (v) such other clinical and administrative duties as may be specified in the Medical Director Agreement.

**(c)** Compensation of the Medical Director shall be as set forth in the Medical Director Agreement. As of the date hereof, the Medical Director Agreement provides for annual compensation of One Hundred Twenty Thousand Dollars (\$120,000.00) for a time commitment of eight (8) hours per month (ninety-six (96) hours per year).

**(d)** The Medical Director Agreement shall automatically renew for successive one-year terms unless terminated by either party upon sixty (60) days\' prior written notice. The compensation and terms of the Medical Director Agreement shall not be subject to modification or amendment without the written consent of the Medical Director and the Manager.

**[Section 5.5 --- Conflicts of Interest]{.underline}**

**(a)** Each Member acknowledges that certain Members and their affiliates may have interests that conflict with the interests of the Center. In particular, the Members acknowledge that: (i) Greenfield Health Partners, LLC is a multispecialty physician group practice that refers patients to the Center and to other healthcare facilities; (ii) Dr. Stein and Dr. Narayan are physicians who practice through Greenfield Health Partners, LLC and who may refer patients to the Center; and (iii) Dr. Stein serves as the Medical Director of the Center pursuant to the Medical Director Agreement.

**(b)** No Member shall be required to refer any patient to the Center, and no Member\'s profit distribution or other rights under this Agreement shall be conditioned upon such Member making any minimum number of referrals to the Center; provided, however, that distributions of Distributable Cash shall be allocated based on Referral Percentage as set forth in Section 4.2.

**(c)** Each Member waives any claim against any other Member for engaging in activities that may compete with or be related to the business of the Center, except to the extent expressly prohibited by this Agreement.

**[ARTICLE VI --- MEMBER OBLIGATIONS]{.underline}**

**[Section 6.1 --- Active Participation]{.underline}**

Each Member who is a physician (or, in the case of Greenfield Health Partners, LLC, the physicians of Greenfield Health Partners, LLC) shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain active medical staff privileges at the Center and to utilize the Center for surgical cases for which the Center is appropriately equipped and staffed. Each Member shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, rules, and regulations, including without limitation the rules and regulations of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services and the Ohio Department of Health.

**[Section 6.2 --- Reporting of Referral Data]{.underline}**

**(a)** Each Member shall cooperate with the Manager in accurately tracking and reporting referral data for purposes of calculating Referral Percentages under Article IV. Each Member shall promptly notify the Manager of any surgical case referred to the Center and shall ensure that referral information is accurately reflected in the Center\'s scheduling and admissions systems.

**(b)** In the case of Greenfield Health Partners, LLC, Greenfield shall cause its individual physicians to accurately report referral information and shall provide the Manager with a quarterly summary identifying each referring physician and the number of Qualified Surgical Case Referrals attributable to such physician during the applicable quarter.

**[ARTICLE VII --- FISCAL MATTERS]{.underline}**

**[Section 7.1 --- Fiscal Year]{.underline}**

The fiscal year of the Center shall be the calendar year.

**[Section 7.2 --- Books and Records; Accounting]{.underline}**

**(a)** The Manager shall maintain or cause to be maintained complete and accurate books and records of the Center, including without limitation records of all surgical cases, referral data, Facility Fee Revenue, and distributions to Members.

**(b)** The Center\'s financial statements shall be prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles and shall be reviewed or audited annually by the Center\'s independent accountant. As of the date hereof, the Center\'s independent accountant is Redstone Accounting Group, LLP.

**(c)** Each Member shall have the right, upon reasonable notice, to inspect and copy the books and records of the Center at the Center\'s principal office during regular business hours.

\[Sections 7.3 through 7.5 omitted --- relating to bank accounts, tax matters, and reporting obligations.\]

**[ARTICLE VIII --- TRANSFER OF MEMBERSHIP INTERESTS]{.underline}**

**Section 8.1 --- Restrictions on Transfer.** No Member may transfer, assign, pledge, or encumber all or any portion of its Membership Interest without the prior written consent of all other Members. Any purported transfer in violation of this Section 8.1 shall be void and of no effect.

\[Remainder of Article VIII omitted --- including right of first refusal, buy-sell provisions, and drag-along/tag-along rights.\]

**[ARTICLE IX --- ADMISSION OF NEW MEMBERS]{.underline}**

\[Article IX omitted in its entirety.\]

**[ARTICLE X --- DISSOLUTION AND WINDING UP]{.underline}**

**Section 10.1 --- Dissolution Distributions.** Upon dissolution of the Center, the assets of the Center shall be liquidated and the proceeds shall be applied: first, to the payment of debts and liabilities of the Center, including amounts owed to Members in their capacity as creditors; second, to the establishment of reserves for contingent liabilities as reasonably determined by the Manager or liquidating agent; and third, to distribution to the Members in proportion to their positive capital account balances as of the date of dissolution.

\[Remainder of Article X omitted.\]

**[ARTICLE XI --- REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES]{.underline}**

**Section 11.1 --- Capacity and Authority.** Each Member represents and warrants that it has the legal capacity and authority to enter into this Agreement and to perform its obligations hereunder.

**Section 11.2 --- No Violations.** Each Member represents and warrants that its execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement does not violate any law, regulation, order, or contractual obligation to which such Member is subject.

**Section 11.3 --- Independent Counsel.** Each Member represents and warrants that it has been advised to seek independent legal counsel regarding the terms of this Agreement, including without limitation the tax, regulatory, and compliance implications of the distribution methodology set forth in Article IV.

\[Remainder of Article XI omitted.\]

**[ARTICLE XII --- GENERAL PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**[Section 12.1 --- Governing Law]{.underline}**

This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Ohio, without regard to principles of conflicts of law.

**[Section 12.2 --- Entire Agreement; Amendment]{.underline}**

**(a)** This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement among the Members with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior agreements and understandings, oral or written, relating to the Center.

**(b)** This Agreement may be amended or modified only by a written instrument signed by all Members.

(Note: As of the date of these excerpts, this Agreement has not been amended since its original effective date of August 22, 2016.)

**[Section 12.3 --- Severability]{.underline}**

\[Section 12.3 omitted.\]

**[Section 12.4 --- Notices]{.underline}**

All notices and other communications under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed given when delivered personally, sent by overnight courier, or mailed by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the following addresses (or to such other address as a Member may designate in writing):

> **Greenfield Health Partners, LLC** 2800 Riverside Medical Plaza, Suite 400 Columbus, OH 43215
>
> Attn: Dr. Raymond K. Stein, M.D., Managing Member
>
> **Dr. Raymond K. Stein, M.D.** c/o Greenfield Health Partners, LLC 2800 Riverside Medical Plaza, Suite 400 Columbus, OH 43215
>
> **Dr. Priya Narayan, M.D.** c/o Greenfield Health Partners, LLC 2800 Riverside Medical Plaza, Suite 400 Columbus, OH 43215

**[Section 12.5 --- Counterparts]{.underline}**

This Agreement may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Execution and delivery of this Agreement by facsimile or electronic transmission shall be deemed effective execution and delivery.

**IN WITNESS WHEREOF**, the Members have executed this Amended and Restated Operating Agreement as of the date first written above.

**GREENFIELD HEALTH PARTNERS, LLC**

By: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**

Name: Dr. Raymond K. Stein, M.D.

Title: Managing Member

Date: August 22, 2016

**DR. RAYMOND K. STEIN, M.D.**, individually

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

Dr. Raymond K. Stein, M.D.

Date: August 22, 2016

**DR. PRIYA NARAYAN, M.D.**, individually

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

Dr. Priya Narayan, M.D.

Date: August 22, 2016

**SCHEDULE OF MEMBERS**

**Address of Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC:** 2850 Riverside Medical Plaza, Suite 100, Columbus, OH 43215

**MEDICAL DIRECTOR AGREEMENT REFERENCE**

The Medical Director Agreement referenced in this Operating Agreement is that certain Medical Director Services Agreement dated as of August 22, 2016, by and between Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC and Dr. Raymond K. Stein, M.D.

**Key Terms:**

> • **Annual Compensation:** \$120,000.00

**[AMENDED AND RESTATED OPERATING AGREEMENT]{.underline}**

**[OF]{.underline}**

**[GREENFIELD HEALTH PARTNERS, LLC]{.underline}**

an Ohio Limited Liability Company

**Effective Date: January 1, 2020**

EXCERPTS --- Selected provisions reproduced for compliance review purposes. Sections not reproduced are indicated by bracketed notation. This document does not constitute the complete Operating Agreement and should be read in conjunction with the full Agreement and all exhibits, schedules, and ancillary documents referenced herein.

**GREENFIELD HEALTH PARTNERS, LLC** 2800 Riverside Medical Plaza, Suite 400 Columbus, OH 43215

EIN: 31-4527893

Originally formed March 14, 2009, pursuant to Ohio Revised Code Chapter 1705 (now Chapter 1706).

This Amended and Restated Operating Agreement (this \"Agreement\") amends, restates, and supersedes in its entirety the Operating Agreement of Greenfield Health Partners, LLC dated March 14, 2009, as previously amended by the First Amendment dated October 1, 2012, the Second Amendment dated August 22, 2016, and the Third Amendment dated January 15, 2018. All terms and conditions of the prior Operating Agreement and its amendments are hereby replaced in their entirety by the terms and conditions set forth herein.

**[PREAMBLE AND RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS**, Greenfield Health Partners, LLC (the \"Company\") was formed on March 14, 2009, as an Ohio limited liability company pursuant to the filing of Articles of Organization with the Ohio Secretary of State under Ohio Revised Code Chapter 1705 (now Chapter 1706), for the purpose of operating a multispecialty physician group practice and related ancillary healthcare services in the Columbus, Ohio metropolitan area;

**WHEREAS**, the Company currently operates twelve (12) clinical locations in the Columbus, Ohio metropolitan area, providing comprehensive medical services across multiple specialties;

**WHEREAS**, the Company currently employs or contracts with eighty-seven (87) physicians, consisting of fifty-two (52) Member physicians and thirty-five (35) employed non-member physicians, practicing across the specialties of Orthopedics, Cardiology, Internal Medicine, Radiology, General Surgery, Urology, and Neurology;

**WHEREAS**, since its formation, the Company has expanded its operations to include investments in affiliated entities, including the Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC, and has entered into various commercial arrangements with healthcare entities operating in the Riverside Medical Plaza and surrounding areas;

**WHEREAS**, the Members desire to amend and restate the Operating Agreement in its entirety to reflect the current membership roster, governance structure, physician compensation methodology, investment arrangements, and distribution mechanisms of the Company, effective as of January 1, 2020;

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Members agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Article I shall have the meanings assigned to them elsewhere in this Agreement.

**\"Affiliated Entity\"** means any entity in which the Company or any Member holds a direct or indirect ownership interest, including without limitation Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC.

**\"Buckeye Investment\"** means the Company\'s sixty percent (60%) membership interest in Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC, an Ohio limited liability company formed on August 22, 2016, located at 2850 Riverside Medical Plaza, Suite 100, Columbus, OH 43215, and any returns, distributions, or other economic benefits derived therefrom.

**\"Compensation Committee\"** means the committee established under Article VII, Section 7.3 of this Agreement, responsible for establishing, overseeing, and administering physician compensation arrangements for the Company.

**\"Employed Physician\"** means a physician employed by the Company pursuant to a written employment agreement who is not a Member and who does not hold any Membership Interest in the Company.

**\"Facility Fee Revenue\"** means gross revenue received by Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC from facility fees billed to patients, third-party payors, and government healthcare programs for surgical cases performed at the Center, prior to deduction of contractual allowances, bad debt, or other adjustments.

**\"Fiscal Year\"** means the twelve-month period commencing January 1 and ending December 31 of each calendar year.

**\"Managing Member\"** means the Member designated under Article VI to manage the day-to-day operations of the Company. As of the effective date of this Agreement, the Managing Member is Dr. Raymond K. Stein, M.D.

**\"Member\"** means an individual physician who holds a Membership Interest in the Company and who has been duly admitted as a member in accordance with Article III of this Agreement.

**\"Membership Interest\"** means a Member\'s ownership interest in the Company, expressed as a percentage of the total outstanding membership interests, as set forth on Exhibit A attached hereto, as amended from time to time.

**\"Net Profits\"** means the net income of the Company for a Fiscal Year as determined in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, consistently applied, as audited by the Company\'s independent auditor (currently Redstone Accounting Group, LLP), after deduction of all expenses, depreciation, amortization, and reserves established pursuant to this Agreement.

**\"Referral Credit\"** means, as further defined in Article VIII, Section 8.4(b), the allocation to an individual Member physician of a portion of Buckeye Investment Returns received by the Company, calculated based on such Member\'s surgical case referrals to Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC during the applicable distribution period.

**[ARTICLE VII --- COMPENSATION]{.underline}**

**Section 7.1 --- General Principles**

All physician compensation arrangements established, maintained, or administered by or on behalf of the Company shall be designed and implemented in a manner consistent with applicable federal and state laws and regulations, including without limitation the Physician Self-Referral Law, 42 U.S.C. § 1395nn (the \"Stark Law\"), the Anti-Kickback Statute, 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7b, the regulations promulgated thereunder, and applicable Ohio laws governing the practice of medicine and physician compensation.

Physician compensation shall be set at fair market value for the services rendered, as determined by periodic independent benchmarking studies. The Company has engaged **Lakeshore Valuation Group, LLC** of Cleveland, Ohio to perform independent compensation benchmarking and fair market value analyses. The most recent comprehensive compensation benchmarking study was completed in **November 2019**, covering the data period 2018--2019, and benchmarked all physician compensation components against the Medical Group Management Association (MGMA) annual compensation surveys, the Sullivan Cotter Physician Compensation and Productivity Survey, and the AMGA Medical Group Compensation and Productivity Survey.

Compensation arrangements shall be periodically reviewed and updated to ensure continued compliance with applicable legal requirements and fair market value standards. The Compensation Committee established under Section 7.3 shall be responsible for overseeing and administering all physician compensation matters.

**Section 7.2 --- Member Physician Compensation**

Each Member physician shall receive compensation from the Company consisting of the following three components:

**(a) Base Salary.** Each Member\'s Base Salary shall be set annually by the Compensation Committee, benchmarked to the 60th percentile of the MGMA annual compensation survey for such Member\'s medical specialty and geographic region (Ohio/Midwest). Base Salary levels shall be reviewed no less frequently than annually by the Compensation Committee and adjusted as appropriate to reflect changes in benchmarking data, individual performance, clinical responsibilities, and market conditions. Base Salary shall be paid in equal semi-monthly installments in accordance with the Company\'s regular payroll schedule.

**(b) Quality Bonus.** Each Member physician shall be eligible for an annual quality bonus of up to twenty-five percent (25%) of such Member\'s Base Salary, determined based on the following criteria and weightings:

> \(i\) **Patient Satisfaction Survey Scores** (weighted 40%): Based on the Member\'s individual patient satisfaction scores as measured by the Company\'s approved patient experience survey instrument, compared against specialty-specific national benchmarks;
>
> \(ii\) **Clinical Quality Metrics** (weighted 40%): Based on the Member\'s performance on clinical quality measures established annually by the Compensation Committee, which may include measures related to preventive care, chronic disease management, surgical outcomes, readmission rates, and other evidence-based quality indicators appropriate to the Member\'s specialty; and
>
> \(iii\) **Medical Records Documentation Compliance** (weighted 20%): Based on the Member\'s compliance with the Company\'s medical records documentation requirements, including timeliness and completeness of clinical notes, coding accuracy, and adherence to documentation standards established by the Compensation Committee.

The Quality Bonus shall be calculated and paid annually, within ninety (90) days following the end of each Fiscal Year, based on the Member\'s performance during such Fiscal Year. The Quality Bonus shall not take into account the volume or value of referrals for designated health services or other services payable by Medicare, Medicaid, or other federal or state healthcare programs.

**(c) Profit Distribution.** In addition to Base Salary and Quality Bonus, each Member physician shall receive annual (and, where applicable, quarterly) profit distributions as provided in Article VIII of this Agreement.

**Section 7.3(a) --- Composition.** The Compensation Committee shall consist of three (3) persons, as follows:

> \(i\) The Managing Member, who shall serve as Chair of the Compensation Committee;
>
> \(ii\) One (1) Member physician elected by majority vote of the Members at the annual meeting of Members, to serve a two-year term; and

>
> \(ii\) Establish and administer the Quality Bonus program for Member physicians under Section 7.2(b), including the selection and weighting of quality metrics;

> \(iv\) Periodically engage an independent valuation firm to conduct fair market value benchmarking studies of physician compensation across all specialties represented by the Company\'s physician workforce, and to review and consider the results of such studies in establishing compensation levels;
>

>
> \(vi\) Report to the Members at each annual meeting of Members on compensation matters, including a summary of compensation levels, benchmarking results, and any material changes to compensation arrangements.

Decisions of the Compensation Committee shall be by majority vote of the Committee members. The Committee may adopt such rules and procedures for the conduct of its business as it deems appropriate, consistent with this Agreement. There are no additional approval requirements applicable to Compensation Committee decisions beyond the majority vote of the Committee itself.

**Section 7.4 --- Compliance Committee**

**Section 7.5 --- Employed Physician Compensation**

**Section 7.5(a) --- Base Salary.** Each Employed Physician\'s Base Salary shall be established by the Managing Member with the approval of the Chief Financial Officer, benchmarked to the 50th percentile of the MGMA annual compensation survey for such Employed Physician\'s medical specialty and geographic region (Ohio/Midwest). Base Salary shall be set forth in each Employed Physician\'s individual written employment agreement with the Company. Adjustments to Employed Physician Base Salary shall be made in the Managing Member\'s discretion, with CFO approval, and shall be documented by written amendment to the applicable employment agreement.

For Internal Medicine physicians, the wRVU threshold shall be four thousand two hundred (4,200) wRVUs per Fiscal Year. For other specialties, thresholds shall be

**[ARTICLE VIII --- DISTRIBUTIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 8.1 --- General Distribution Policy**

The Company shall make distributions of Net Profits to the Members no less frequently than annually, following the close of each Fiscal Year, after payment of all Company obligations (including physician compensation under Article VII), establishment of reasonable reserves as determined by the Chief Financial Officer in consultation with the Managing Member, and satisfaction of all withholding and tax deposit requirements. Distributions shall be made in accordance with the provisions of this Article VIII.

**Section 8.2 --- Standard Profit Distributions**

Net Profits of the Company (excluding Buckeye Investment Returns, which are governed exclusively by Section 8.4 below) shall be distributed to the Members **in proportion to each Member\'s Membership Interest percentage** as set forth on Exhibit A, as in effect on the last day of the Fiscal Year for which such distribution is made.

By way of illustration: a Member holding a 4.2% Membership Interest shall receive 4.2% of distributable Net Profits under this Section 8.2; a Member holding a 3.1% Membership Interest shall receive 3.1% of distributable Net Profits under this Section 8.2.

Standard profit distributions under this Section 8.2 shall be allocated solely based on Membership Interest percentages and shall not be based on, or take into account, the volume or value of referrals for designated health services or other services payable by Medicare, Medicaid, or other federal or state healthcare programs. The allocation of standard profit distributions under this Section 8.2 is determined exclusively by each Member\'s ownership percentage and bears no relationship to such Member\'s individual clinical productivity, patient referral patterns, or utilization of the Company\'s services or the services of any Affiliated Entity.

**Section 8.3 --- Tax Distributions**

The Company shall make quarterly estimated tax distributions to each Member in amounts reasonably estimated by the CFO to be sufficient to cover such Member\'s federal and state income tax liability attributable to such Member\'s allocable share of Company income for the applicable quarter. Tax distributions shall be treated as advances against the annual profit distribution to which such Member is entitled under Section 8.2. In the event that tax distributions made to a Member during a Fiscal Year exceed such Member\'s total distribution entitlement for such year, the excess shall be treated as a loan from the Company to such Member, repayable upon demand.

**Section 8.4 --- Buckeye Investment Returns**

**Section 8.4(a) --- Entity-Level Distribution from Buckeye Surgical Center.** The Company holds a sixty percent (60%) membership interest in Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC, an Ohio limited liability company formed August 22, 2016. Distributions received by the Company from Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC (collectively, \"Buckeye Investment Returns\") shall be allocated among the Members in accordance with this Section 8.4, and **shall NOT be allocated in accordance with the standard Membership Interest percentages** set forth in Section 8.2.

Pursuant to the Operating Agreement of Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC (the \"Buckeye Operating Agreement,\" a separate agreement on file with the Company), distributions from Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC to its members are made in proportion to each member\'s surgical case referral volume to the Center, adjusted quarterly. The Company\'s sixty percent (60%) share of Buckeye distributions is received by the Company as a single distribution and thereafter allocated internally to the Members in accordance with Section 8.4(b) below.

Separately, the following Members hold personal membership interests in Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC, which are separate from and in addition to the Company\'s sixty percent (60%) interest:

> • Dr. Raymond K. Stein, M.D. --- 25% personal membership interest
>
> • Dr. Priya Narayan, M.D. --- 15% personal membership interest

Distributions received by Dr. Stein and Dr. Narayan on account of their personal membership interests in Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC are governed exclusively by the Buckeye Operating Agreement and are not subject to this Agreement.

**Section 8.4(b) --- Referral Credit Mechanism.** Buckeye Investment Returns received by the Company shall be allocated among the Members based on each Member\'s Referral Credits for the applicable distribution period. Each Member who refers a surgical case to Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC during a Fiscal Year shall receive a Referral Credit equal to **one-half of one percent (0.5%) of the Facility Fee Revenue** generated by such referred case. Referral Credits shall be calculated quarterly based on surgical case data provided by the Administrator of Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC and shall be reconciled annually following the close of each Fiscal Year.

The aggregate Referral Credits allocated to all referring Members for a Fiscal Year shall be deducted from the total Buckeye Investment Returns received by the Company for such Fiscal Year. Any remainder of Buckeye Investment Returns after allocation of Referral Credits shall be distributed to all Members in proportion to their Membership Interest percentages under Section 8.2.

By way of illustration: If Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC performs nine hundred (900) surgical cases in a Fiscal Year with an average Facility Fee of Eight Thousand Two Hundred Dollars (\$8,200) per case, total Facility Fee Revenue would equal Seven Million Three Hundred Eighty Thousand Dollars (\$7,380,000) (900 × \$8,200). Total Referral Credits would equal Thirty-Six Thousand Nine Hundred Dollars (\$36,900) (\$7,380,000 × 0.5%). A Member who refers one hundred (100) cases generating Eight Hundred Twenty Thousand Dollars (\$820,000) in Facility Fee Revenue would receive Referral Credits of Four Thousand One Hundred Dollars (\$4,100) (\$820,000 × 0.5%).

The Referral Credit mechanism is intended to recognize the value contributed by referring Members to the Buckeye Investment and to align Member incentives with the success of the Company\'s affiliated surgical center. The Referral Credit allocation shall be calculated by the CFO and shall be subject to quarterly review by the Compensation Committee.

**Section 8.4(c) --- Reporting.** The Chief Financial Officer shall prepare and distribute to each Member a quarterly statement setting forth: (i) total Buckeye Investment Returns received by the Company during such quarter; (ii) each Member\'s Referral Credits calculated for such quarter, including the number of referred cases and associated Facility Fee Revenue; and (iii) each Member\'s share of the remainder distributed under the standard Membership Interest percentages set forth in Section 8.2. An annual reconciliation of Referral Credits and Buckeye Investment Returns shall be completed within ninety (90) days following the end of each Fiscal Year and shall be distributed to all Members together with the annual audit report.

**Section 8.5 --- Limitations on Distributions**

No distribution shall be made to any Member if, after giving effect to such distribution, the Company would be unable to pay its debts as they become due in the ordinary course of business, or if the Company\'s total liabilities (other than liabilities to Members on account of their Membership Interests) would exceed the fair value of the Company\'s total assets. All distributions are subject to applicable federal and state tax withholding requirements and to such reserves as the CFO determines to be reasonably necessary for the Company\'s operations and obligations.

23	As used in this Lease, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below:
24	
25	**\"Base Rent\"** shall mean the annual rental amount specified in Article IV of this Lease.

27	**\"Building\"** shall mean the medical office building located at 2800 Riverside Medical Plaza, Columbus, OH 43215, including all improvements, fixtures, and appurtenances thereto.

30

41	**Section 2.1 --- Lease of Premises.** Landlord hereby leases to Tenant, and Tenant hereby leases from Landlord, the Premises consisting of approximately three thousand two hundred (3,200) square feet of medical office space designated as Suite 210 in the Building. The exact dimensions, boundaries, and layout of the Premises are as set forth on the floor plan attached hereto as **Exhibit A**.
