43	**Section 2.2 --- Permitted Use.** Tenant shall use and occupy the Premises solely for the Permitted Use, namely the operation of a diagnostic imaging center providing MRI, CT, X-ray, ultrasound, and related diagnostic imaging services, and for no other purpose without the prior written consent of Landlord. Tenant shall obtain and maintain, at Tenant\'s sole cost and expense, all licenses, permits, certificates of need, and certifications required for the lawful operation of a diagnostic imaging facility in the State of Ohio.
44	
45	**Section 2.3 --- Compliance with Laws.** Tenant shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, statutes, ordinances, regulations, codes, and requirements in its use and occupancy of the Premises, including without limitation all health care regulatory requirements applicable to the operation of a diagnostic imaging center.
46	
47	**Section 2.4 --- Common Areas.** Tenant and its employees, agents, patients, and invitees shall have the non-exclusive right to use the Common Areas of the Building in common with Landlord, other tenants, and their respective employees, agents, patients, and invitees, subject to such reasonable rules and regulations as Landlord may adopt from time to time.
48	
49	**[ARTICLE III --- TERM]{.underline}**

51	**Section 3.1 --- Initial Term.** The initial term of this Lease shall commence on January 1, 2021 (the \"Commencement Date\") and shall expire on December 31, 2025 (the \"Expiration Date\"), unless sooner terminated in accordance with the provisions of this Lease. The initial term shall consist of five (5) Lease Years.
52	
53	**Section 3.2 --- Renewal Option.** Tenant shall have one (1) option to renew this Lease for an additional term of three (3) years (the \"Renewal Term\"), commencing on January 1, 2026 and expiring on December 31, 2028, upon written notice delivered to Landlord not less than one hundred eighty (180) days prior to the Expiration Date. The Renewal Term shall be upon the same terms and conditions as set forth herein, except that Base Rent during the Renewal Term shall be at a rate mutually agreed upon by the parties in good faith. If the parties are unable to agree upon the Renewal Term rent within sixty (60) days after Tenant\'s exercise of the renewal option, either party may withdraw from the renewal by written notice to the other.
54	
55	**Section 3.3 --- Holdover.** If Tenant remains in possession of the Premises after the expiration or termination of this Lease without executing a renewal or new lease agreement, Tenant shall be deemed a tenant at sufferance and shall pay Base Rent at a rate equal to one hundred fifty percent (150%) of the then-current monthly Base Rent, on a month-to-month basis, terminable by either party upon thirty (30) days\' prior written notice. Such holdover tenancy shall otherwise be subject to all of the terms and conditions of this Lease.
56	
57	**[ARTICLE IV --- RENT]{.underline}**
58	
59	**Section 4.1 --- Base Rent.** Tenant shall pay to Landlord annual Base Rent in the amount of Fifty-Seven Thousand Six Hundred Dollars (\$57,600.00), calculated at the rate of Eighteen Dollars (\$18.00) per rentable square foot per year for the three thousand two hundred (3,200) square feet of the Premises (\$18.00 × 3,200 sq. ft. = \$57,600.00 per annum).
60	
61	**Section 4.2 --- Monthly Installments.** Base Rent shall be payable in equal monthly installments of Four Thousand Eight Hundred Dollars (\$4,800.00) each, due and payable in advance on the first (1st) day of each calendar month during the Term, without notice, demand, setoff, or deduction of any kind. Payment shall be made to Landlord at the address set forth in Article XVI or to such other address as Landlord may designate in writing.
62	
63	**Section 4.3 --- Fixed Rate.** Base Rent shall remain fixed at the rate set forth in Section 4.1 for the entire Initial Term.
64	
65	**Section 4.4 --- Late Payment.** If any installment of Base Rent or any other sum due under this Lease is not received by Landlord within ten (10) business days after the date on which such payment is due, Tenant shall pay a late fee equal to five percent (5%) of the overdue amount, plus interest at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month (or the maximum rate permitted by law, whichever is less) on the unpaid balance from the date due until the date paid.
66	
67	**Section 4.5 --- Additional Rent.** In addition to Base Rent, Tenant shall pay as Additional Rent Tenant\'s proportionate share of Operating Expenses for the Building, as more particularly set forth in Article V. Any sums payable by Tenant under this Lease, other than Base Rent, shall be deemed Additional Rent for all purposes hereunder.
68	
69	**Section 4.6 --- Rent Commencement.** Rent shall commence on the Commencement Date. No rent abatement, free rent period, or rent concession is provided under this Lease.
70

72	
73	**Section 5.1 --- Operating Expenses Defined.** As used herein, \"Operating Expenses\" shall mean all costs and expenses incurred by Landlord in owning, operating, managing, maintaining, and repairing the Building and Common Areas, including without limitation: real property taxes and assessments; property and casualty insurance premiums; common area maintenance; utilities for Common Areas; landscaping; snow removal; janitorial services for Common Areas; building management fees; and repairs and maintenance of the Building\'s structural components, roof, exterior walls, HVAC systems, elevators, and parking areas.
74	
75	**Section 5.2 --- Tenant\'s Proportionate Share.** Tenant\'s proportionate share of Operating Expenses shall be calculated based on the ratio of the rentable square footage of the Premises (3,200 sq. ft.) to the total leasable square footage of the Building, as more particularly set forth on **Exhibit B** attached hereto. Landlord shall provide Tenant with an annual written estimate of Operating Expenses prior to the commencement of each calendar year, and Tenant shall pay one-twelfth (1/12) of its estimated proportionate share monthly, concurrent with payment of Base Rent.
76	
77	**Section 5.3 --- Annual Reconciliation.** Within ninety (90) days after the end of each calendar year, Landlord shall furnish Tenant with a written statement of actual Operating Expenses incurred during such year. If Tenant\'s payments are less than Tenant\'s proportionate share of actual Operating Expenses, Tenant shall pay the deficiency to Landlord within thirty (30) days of receipt of such statement.
78	
79	**Section 5.4 --- Exclusions from Operating Expenses.** Operating Expenses shall not include: capital improvements (except those required by governmental regulation enacted after the Effective Date or those reasonably expected to reduce Operating Expenses); leasing commissions and brokerage fees; mortgage principal and interest payments; Landlord\'s income taxes; costs of tenant improvements for individual tenants; or costs incurred due to Landlord\'s negligence.

Within thirty (30) days after the expiration or termination of this Lease and Tenant\'s surrender of the Premises, Landlord shall return to Tenant the Security Deposit, less any amounts lawfully applied. Landlord shall have no obligation to pay interest on the Security Deposit.

111	**Section 10.1 --- Tenant\'s Indemnification.** Tenant shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Landlord and its members, managers, officers, agents, and employees from and against all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising out of or related to: (a) Tenant\'s use or occupancy of the Premises; (b) any act, omission, or negligence of Tenant, its employees, agents, contractors, patients, or invitees; or (c) any breach of this Lease by Tenant.

113	**Section 10.2 --- Landlord\'s Indemnification.** Landlord shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Tenant and its members, managers, officers, agents, and employees from and against all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising out of or related to: (a) Landlord\'s negligence or willful misconduct; or (b) any breach of this Lease by Landlord.
114	
115	**Section 10.3 --- Limitation of Liability.** In no event shall either party be liable to the other for any consequential, incidental, indirect, special, or punitive damages arising out of or related to this Lease, regardless of whether such damages are based on contract, tort, strict liability, or any other theory.
116	
117	**[ARTICLE XI --- ASSIGNMENT AND SUBLETTING]{.underline}**
118	
119	Tenant shall not assign this Lease or any interest herein, nor sublet the Premises or any part thereof, nor permit the use of the Premises by any party other than Tenant, without the prior written consent of Landlord, which consent may be withheld in Landlord\'s sole and absolute discretion. Any attempted assignment, subletting, or transfer without such consent shall be null and void and shall constitute a default under this Lease. In the event of a permitted assignment, Tenant shall remain jointly and severally liable with the assignee for all obligations under this Lease for the remainder of the Term.
120	
121	**[ARTICLE XII --- DEFAULT AND REMEDIES]{.underline}**
122	
123	**Section 12.1 --- Events of Default.** Each of the following shall constitute an Event of Default under this Lease: (a) Tenant\'s failure to pay Base Rent or Additional Rent within ten (10) days after written notice from Landlord that such payment is overdue; (b) Tenant\'s breach of any non-monetary covenant, condition, or obligation under this Lease that remains uncured for thirty (30) days after written notice from Landlord specifying such breach; (c) the filing by or against Tenant of a petition in bankruptcy, or Tenant\'s insolvency, assignment for the benefit of creditors, or appointment of a receiver; or (d) Tenant\'s abandonment of the Premises.
124	
125	**Section 12.2 --- Landlord\'s Remedies.** Upon the occurrence of an Event of Default, Landlord may, at its option: (a) terminate this Lease by written notice to Tenant, whereupon Tenant shall immediately surrender the Premises; (b) re-enter and repossess the Premises; (c) recover from Tenant all unpaid rent, Additional Rent, and other sums due through the date of termination; and (d) accelerate all remaining Base Rent and Additional Rent due for the balance of the Term, discounted to present value at a rate of four percent (4%) per annum, less the fair rental value of the Premises for such period.

127	**Section 12.3 --- Tenant\'s Remedies.** If Landlord fails to perform any material obligation under this Lease, Tenant shall provide Landlord with written notice specifying the nature of such default. If Landlord fails to cure such default within thirty (30) days after receipt of such notice (or, if the default cannot reasonably be cured within thirty days, fails to commence cure and diligently pursue the same to completion), Tenant may, at its option, terminate this Lease upon thirty (30) days\' additional written notice or pursue any remedies available at law or in equity.
128	
129	**[ARTICLE XIII --- CASUALTY AND CONDEMNATION]{.underline}**
130	
131	**Section 13.1 --- Casualty.** If the Premises are damaged or destroyed by fire or other casualty, Landlord shall notify Tenant within thirty (30) days of such event whether restoration can be completed within one hundred eighty (180) days. If restoration cannot be completed within one hundred eighty (180) days, either party may terminate this Lease upon thirty (30) days\' written notice to the other.
132	
133	**Section 13.2 --- Condemnation.** If all or a substantial portion of the Premises is taken by eminent domain or condemnation, this Lease shall terminate as of the date of such taking, and rent shall be apportioned to the date of termination. If only a portion of the Premises is taken and the remaining portion is reasonably suitable for Tenant\'s continued use, the Lease shall continue and Base Rent shall be reduced proportionately based on the square footage taken.

136	
137	This Lease shall be subordinate to any mortgage, deed of trust, or other security instrument now or hereafter placed upon the Building or the property on which it is situated. Tenant shall execute and deliver such subordination, non-disturbance, and attornment agreements as may be reasonably requested by Landlord or Landlord\'s lender within fifteen (15) days of such request. Each party agrees to execute and deliver to the other, within fifteen (15) days of written request, an estoppel certificate confirming the status of this Lease, the absence of defaults, and such other matters as may reasonably be requested.

144	
145	**Section 15.3 --- Independent Operations.** Tenant represents and warrants that ClearView Diagnostic Imaging, LLC is independently owned and operated, and that no physician, physician group, hospital, or other health care entity (other than ClearView Diagnostic Imaging, LLC and its members) has any direct or indirect ownership interest or financial interest in Tenant.
146	
147	**Section 15.4 --- Regulatory Compliance.** Tenant acknowledges and agrees that it is solely responsible for compliance with all federal and state health care laws and regulations applicable to its diagnostic imaging operations at the Premises, including but not limited to Medicare and Medicaid participation requirements, applicable state licensure and certification requirements, and radiation safety regulations.
148

169	Notices shall be effective upon receipt if delivered by hand or overnight courier, or three (3) business days after deposit in the United States mail if sent by certified mail. Either party may change its notice address by written notice to the other party in accordance with this Article.
170	
171	**[ARTICLE XVII --- MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS]{.underline}**
172	
173	**Section 17.1 --- Entire Agreement.** This Lease, together with the Exhibits attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations, understandings, and agreements, whether oral or written.
174	
175	**Section 17.2 --- Amendments.** This Lease may not be amended, modified, or supplemented except by a written instrument duly executed by both parties.
176	
177	**Section 17.3 --- Governing Law.** This Lease shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Ohio, without regard to its conflict of laws principles.
178	
179	**Section 17.4 --- Venue.** Any action or proceeding arising out of or related to this Lease shall be brought exclusively in the state or federal courts located in Franklin County, Ohio, and each party hereby consents to the jurisdiction of such courts.
180	
181	**Section 17.5 --- Severability.** If any provision of this Lease is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable by a court of competent jurisdiction, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect, and the invalid provision shall be modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it valid and enforceable.
182	
183	**Section 17.6 --- Waiver.** No waiver by either party of any breach or default of any term, covenant, or condition of this Lease shall be deemed a waiver of any subsequent breach or default, whether of the same or different provision.

Each party shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other party from and against any claims for brokerage commissions, finder\'s fees, or similar compensation arising from a breach of this representation.

**[COMMERCIAL LEASE AGREEMENT]{.underline}**

**2800 Riverside Medical Plaza** **Columbus, Ohio 43215**

This Commercial Lease Agreement (this \"Lease\") is entered into as of March 1, 2022 (the \"Effective Date\"), by and between **GREENFIELD HEALTH PARTNERS, LLC**, an Ohio limited liability company (\"Landlord\"), and **PINNACLE REFERENCE LABORATORY, INC.**, an Ohio corporation (\"Tenant\").

**RECITALS**

**WHEREAS**, Landlord is the owner and operator of certain medical office space located at 2800 Riverside Medical Plaza, Columbus, Ohio 43215, a multi-tenant medical office building (the \"Building\"); and

**WHEREAS**, Tenant is an independent clinical reference laboratory engaged in the business of providing laboratory testing and analysis services to healthcare providers and other clients; and

**WHEREAS**, Tenant desires to lease from Landlord, and Landlord desires to lease to Tenant, certain premises within the Building for the purpose of operating a clinical reference laboratory and related administrative functions, on the terms and conditions set forth herein;

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

As used in this Lease, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below:

**\"Additional Rent\"** shall mean all amounts payable by Tenant under this Lease other than Base Rent, including without limitation Tenant\'s proportionate share of increases in real estate taxes and operating expenses.

**\"Base Rent\"** shall mean Twenty-Two Dollars (\$22.00) per rentable square foot per annum, as more particularly described in Article III.

**\"Building\"** shall mean 2800 Riverside Medical Plaza, Columbus, OH 43215, including all improvements, common areas, and appurtenances thereto.

**\"Commencement Date\"** shall mean March 1, 2022.

**\"Expiration Date\"** shall mean February 28, 2025.

**\"FMV Appraisal\"** or **\"Appraisal\"** shall mean that certain fair market value appraisal report prepared by Lakeshore Valuation Group, LLC, dated September 15, 2020 (the \"Lakeshore Appraisal\"), appraising rental rates for medical office space at the Building, a summary of which is attached hereto as Exhibit B.

**\"Landlord\"** shall mean Greenfield Health Partners, LLC, an Ohio limited liability company, with principal offices at 2800 Riverside Medical Plaza, Suite 400, Columbus, OH 43215 (EIN: 31-4527893).

**\"Lease Term\"** shall mean the three (3) year period commencing on the Commencement Date and expiring on the Expiration Date, unless earlier terminated in accordance with the terms of this Lease.

**\"Permitted Use\"** shall mean the operation of a clinical reference laboratory and related administrative functions.

**\"Premises\"** shall mean Suite 105, consisting of approximately 1,800 rentable square feet, located at 2800 Riverside Medical Plaza, Columbus, OH 43215, as more particularly depicted on Exhibit A attached hereto.

**\"Tenant\"** shall mean Pinnacle Reference Laboratory, Inc., an Ohio corporation.

**\"Tenant\'s CEO\"** shall mean Sandra Cho.

**[ARTICLE II --- PREMISES AND LEASE TERM]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1 --- Premises.** Landlord hereby leases to Tenant, and Tenant hereby leases from Landlord, the Premises, consisting of Suite 105 at 2800 Riverside Medical Plaza, Columbus, OH 43215, containing approximately 1,800 rentable square feet, as more particularly depicted on Exhibit A attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference. The Premises are located on the first floor of the Building. Tenant shall have the non-exclusive right, in common with other tenants and occupants of the Building, to use the common areas of the Building, including lobbies, corridors, restrooms, elevators, stairways, and parking facilities, subject to the reasonable rules and regulations established by Landlord from time to time.

**Section 2.2 --- Lease Term.** The Lease Term shall be three (3) years, commencing on March 1, 2022 (the \"Commencement Date\") and expiring on February 28, 2025 (the \"Expiration Date\"), unless earlier terminated in accordance with the terms of this Lease. Upon the expiration or earlier termination of the Lease Term, Tenant shall surrender the Premises to Landlord in the condition required by this Lease.

**Section 2.3 --- Condition of Premises.** Tenant acknowledges that Tenant has inspected the Premises and accepts the Premises in their current \"as-is\" condition as of the Commencement Date. Landlord has made no representations or warranties regarding the condition, suitability, or fitness of the Premises for any particular purpose except as expressly set forth herein. Landlord shall deliver the Premises to Tenant in broom-clean condition on the Commencement Date.

**Section 2.4 --- Permitted Use.** Tenant shall use and occupy the Premises solely for the Permitted Use (operation of a clinical reference laboratory and related administrative functions) and for no other purpose without the prior written consent of Landlord, which consent may be withheld in Landlord\'s reasonable discretion. Tenant shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, rules, regulations, and ordinances in connection with Tenant\'s use and occupancy of the Premises, including without limitation all Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (\"CLIA\") certification requirements and all State of Ohio laboratory licensure requirements.

**[ARTICLE III --- RENT]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- Base Rent.** Tenant shall pay to Landlord annual Base Rent of Thirty-Nine Thousand Six Hundred Dollars (\$39,600.00), calculated at a rate of Twenty-Two Dollars (\$22.00) per rentable square foot per annum (1,800 sq. ft. × \$22.00/sq. ft. = \$39,600.00/year). Base Rent shall be payable in equal monthly installments of Three Thousand Three Hundred Dollars (\$3,300.00) each, due and payable in advance on the first (1st) day of each calendar month during the Lease Term. If the Commencement Date falls on a day other than the first day of a calendar month, the Base Rent for such partial month shall be prorated on a per diem basis. All payments of Base Rent shall be made to Landlord at the address set forth in Section 12.2, or to such other address as Landlord may designate in writing from time to time, without demand, notice, offset, or deduction of any kind.

**Section 3.2 --- FMV Determination.** The parties acknowledge and agree that the Base Rent has been established with reference to the fair market value of comparable medical office space in the Columbus, Ohio metropolitan area as determined by the Lakeshore Appraisal (that certain fair market value appraisal prepared by Lakeshore Valuation Group, LLC, dated September 15, 2020). A copy of the summary of the Lakeshore Appraisal is attached hereto as Exhibit B and incorporated herein by reference. The parties have reviewed the Lakeshore Appraisal and have agreed upon the Base Rent set forth in Section 3.1 based upon their review of such appraisal and their knowledge of the local commercial real estate market.

**Section 3.3 --- No Escalation.** The Base Rent shall remain fixed at Twenty-Two Dollars (\$22.00) per rentable square foot per annum throughout the entire Lease Term. There shall be no annual escalation, adjustment, or increase to the Base Rent during the Lease Term.

**Section 3.4 --- Additional Rent.** In addition to Base Rent, Tenant shall pay, as Additional Rent, Tenant\'s proportionate share of increases in real estate taxes and operating expenses for the Building over base year 2022 amounts. Tenant\'s proportionate share shall be calculated as the ratio of the rentable area of the Premises (1,800 square feet) to the total rentable area of the Building. Landlord shall provide Tenant with a statement of estimated Additional Rent for each calendar year and a reconciliation statement following the close of each calendar year. Any underpayment shall be due within thirty (30) days of Tenant\'s receipt of the reconciliation statement; any overpayment shall be credited against the next installment(s) of Additional Rent.

**Section 3.5 --- Late Charges.** If any installment of Base Rent or Additional Rent is not received by Landlord within ten (10) days after the date on which such payment is due, Tenant shall pay to Landlord a late charge equal to five percent (5%) of the overdue amount. Such late charge shall constitute liquidated damages and shall be payable as Additional Rent. The imposition of a late charge shall not constitute a waiver of Landlord\'s right to pursue any other remedy available under this Lease or at law.

**Section 3.6 --- Independent Determination.** The parties represent and warrant that the Base Rent set forth herein was determined through arm\'s-length negotiation between unrelated parties and does not take into account the volume or value of any referrals or other business generated between the parties, or between any physician or healthcare provider affiliated with Landlord and Tenant. The rental rate reflects a commercially reasonable rate for the Premises and the services and amenities provided by Landlord hereunder.

**[ARTICLE IV --- SECURITY DEPOSIT]{.underline}**

**Section 4.1 --- Security Deposit.** Upon execution of this Lease, Tenant has deposited with Landlord the sum of Six Thousand Six Hundred Dollars (\$6,600.00) as a security deposit (the \"Security Deposit\"), which amount is equal to two (2) months\' Base Rent. The Security Deposit shall be held by Landlord as security for the faithful performance by Tenant of all terms, covenants, and conditions of this Lease.

**Section 4.2 --- Application and Return.** If Tenant defaults in the performance of any provision of this Lease, Landlord may use, apply, or retain all or any portion of the Security Deposit to compensate Landlord for any loss or damage resulting from such default, including without limitation unpaid rent, repair costs, and cleaning expenses. In the event Landlord applies any portion of the Security Deposit, Tenant shall, within ten (10) days of written demand, deposit with Landlord an amount sufficient to restore the Security Deposit to its full amount. Provided Tenant has fully performed all of its obligations under this Lease, Landlord shall return the Security Deposit (or the balance thereof remaining after any permitted deductions) to Tenant within thirty (30) days following the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease and Tenant\'s surrender of the Premises.

**[ARTICLE V --- UTILITIES AND SERVICES]{.underline}**

**Section 5.1 --- Landlord-Provided Services.** Landlord shall provide the following standard building services during the Lease Term: (a) heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (\"HVAC\") to the Premises during normal business hours (7:00 AM to 7:00 PM, Monday through Friday, excluding federally recognized holidays); (b) hot and cold water for lavatory and drinking purposes from existing Building supply lines; (c) sewer service; (d) trash removal from designated collection areas; (e) elevator service (if applicable); and (f) maintenance of common areas, including lobbies, corridors, restrooms, and parking facilities. After-hours HVAC service shall be available upon Tenant\'s request, at Tenant\'s expense, at the prevailing rate established by Landlord from time to time.

**Section 5.2 --- Tenant Utilities.** Tenant shall be responsible for and shall pay directly to the applicable utility provider(s) the cost of all separately metered electricity to the Premises. Tenant acknowledges that laboratory operations may require above-standard electrical capacity, and any costs associated with electrical upgrades, supplemental wiring, dedicated circuits, or additional capacity to serve the Premises shall be Tenant\'s sole responsibility, subject to Landlord\'s prior written approval of any modifications to Building electrical systems.

**Section 5.3 --- Janitorial Services.** Landlord shall provide standard janitorial service to the Premises five (5) days per week (Monday through Friday). Tenant may, at Tenant\'s sole expense, arrange for specialized laboratory cleaning services as may be required for Tenant\'s laboratory operations. Tenant shall coordinate any specialized cleaning with Landlord\'s janitorial schedule to avoid interference with Building operations.

**[ARTICLE VI --- MAINTENANCE AND REPAIRS]{.underline}**

**Section 6.1 --- Landlord Maintenance.** Landlord shall be responsible for the repair and maintenance of the structural elements of the Building, including the roof, foundation, exterior walls, load-bearing walls, and common areas, as well as the maintenance and repair of the Building\'s mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and HVAC systems (exclusive of any supplemental systems installed by Tenant). Landlord shall maintain the common areas of the Building in a clean, safe, and orderly condition consistent with the operation of a first-class medical office building.

**Section 6.2 --- Tenant Maintenance.** Tenant shall, at Tenant\'s sole cost and expense, maintain the interior of the Premises in good order, condition, and repair throughout the Lease Term, including without limitation all non-structural repairs, interior painting, floor coverings, interior doors, and any laboratory fixtures, equipment, or supplemental systems installed by Tenant. Tenant shall promptly notify Landlord of any condition within the Premises that may require repair or maintenance by Landlord under Section 6.1.

**Section 6.3 --- Alterations.** Tenant shall not make any alterations, additions, or improvements to the Premises without the prior written consent of Landlord, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. All alterations shall be performed in a good and workmanlike manner, in compliance with all applicable laws and building codes, and at Tenant\'s sole cost and expense. Any approved alterations, additions, or improvements (other than Tenant\'s trade fixtures and removable equipment) shall become the property of Landlord upon the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease, unless Landlord notifies Tenant in writing at the time of approval (or prior to the expiration of the Lease Term) that Landlord requires Tenant to remove such alterations and restore the Premises to their original condition.

**[ARTICLE VII --- INSURANCE AND INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**

**Section 7.1 --- Tenant\'s Insurance.** Tenant shall procure and maintain in force throughout the Lease Term the following insurance coverages:

> \(a\) Commercial general liability insurance with limits of not less than One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000.00) per occurrence and Two Million Dollars (\$2,000,000.00) in the aggregate, naming Landlord as an additional insured;
>
> \(b\) Property insurance covering Tenant\'s personal property, furniture, fixtures, equipment, laboratory instruments, and improvements, in an amount not less than the full replacement cost thereof;
>
> \(c\) Workers\' compensation insurance as required by the laws of the State of Ohio, with employer\'s liability limits of not less than Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000.00) per occurrence; and
>
> \(d\) Professional liability insurance appropriate for clinical laboratory operations, with limits of not less than One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000.00) per occurrence and Two Million Dollars (\$2,000,000.00) in the aggregate.

Tenant shall deliver to Landlord certificates of insurance evidencing all required coverages prior to the Commencement Date and upon each renewal thereof.

**Section 7.2 --- Landlord\'s Insurance.** Landlord shall maintain property insurance on the Building in an amount not less than the full replacement cost thereof, and commercial general liability insurance with commercially reasonable limits.

**Section 7.3 --- Mutual Waiver of Subrogation.** Landlord and Tenant each hereby waive any and all rights of recovery, claim, action, or cause of action against the other for any loss or damage to property covered by valid and collectible property insurance policies, to the extent of any recovery under such policies. Each party shall cause its insurance carriers to include a waiver of subrogation endorsement in all applicable policies.

**Section 7.4 --- Indemnification.** Tenant shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Landlord and its members, managers, officers, agents, and employees from and against any and all claims, demands, liabilities, damages, losses, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising from or related to (a) Tenant\'s use or occupancy of the Premises, (b) the conduct of Tenant\'s business, (c) any activity, work, or thing done, permitted, or suffered by Tenant in or about the Premises, or (d) any negligence or willful misconduct of Tenant or its agents, employees, or contractors. Landlord shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Tenant and its officers, directors, agents, and employees from and against any and all claims, demands, liabilities, damages, losses, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising from or related to (a) Landlord\'s negligence or willful misconduct, or (b) Landlord\'s breach of any obligation under this Lease.

**[ARTICLE VIII --- ASSIGNMENT AND SUBLETTING]{.underline}**

**Section 8.1 --- Restriction on Transfer.** Tenant shall not assign, transfer, mortgage, pledge, hypothecate, or encumber this Lease, in whole or in part, nor sublet the Premises or any portion thereof, nor permit the Premises or any part thereof to be used or occupied by any person or entity other than Tenant, without the prior written consent of Landlord, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. Any purported assignment, transfer, or subletting without Landlord\'s prior written consent shall be void and of no force or effect and shall constitute an Event of Default under this Lease. Landlord\'s consent to any one assignment or sublease shall not constitute a waiver of the requirement of Landlord\'s consent to any subsequent assignment or sublease.

**[ARTICLE IX --- DEFAULT AND REMEDIES]{.underline}**

**Section 9.1 --- Events of Default.** The occurrence of any of the following shall constitute an \"Event of Default\" by Tenant under this Lease:

> \(a\) Tenant\'s failure to pay any installment of Base Rent, Additional Rent, or any other sum due under this Lease within ten (10) days after Landlord delivers written notice of such failure to Tenant;
>
> \(b\) Tenant\'s failure to perform or observe any other term, covenant, or condition of this Lease, if such failure continues for thirty (30) days after Landlord delivers written notice thereof to Tenant; provided, however, that if the nature of such default is such that it cannot reasonably be cured within thirty (30) days, Tenant shall not be in default if Tenant commences to cure such default within such thirty (30) day period and thereafter diligently pursues such cure to completion;
>
> \(c\) The filing by or against Tenant of any petition under the United States Bankruptcy Code or any similar federal or state insolvency statute, the appointment of a receiver or trustee for Tenant\'s assets, or the making by Tenant of a general assignment for the benefit of creditors; or
>
> \(d\) The revocation, suspension, or non-renewal of any license, certification, or accreditation required for Tenant to conduct clinical laboratory operations at the Premises, including without limitation CLIA certification or Ohio laboratory licensure.

**Section 9.2 --- Landlord\'s Remedies.** Upon the occurrence of an Event of Default, Landlord may, at Landlord\'s option, exercise any one or more of the following remedies: (a) terminate this Lease by delivering written notice of termination to Tenant; (b) re-enter the Premises and remove all persons and property therefrom; (c) accelerate all Base Rent and Additional Rent remaining due for the balance of the Lease Term; and (d) pursue any other remedy available at law or in equity under the laws of the State of Ohio.

**Section 9.3 --- Landlord\'s Default.** If Landlord fails to perform any obligation under this Lease, Tenant shall deliver written notice of such failure to Landlord. Landlord shall have thirty (30) days after receipt of such notice to cure such failure, or such longer period as may be reasonably necessary to effect a cure, provided Landlord commences such cure within such thirty (30) day period and diligently pursues the same to completion.

**[ARTICLE X --- COMPLIANCE WITH LAWS; REGULATORY PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 10.1 --- General Compliance.** Both parties shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, rules, regulations, ordinances, and governmental orders in connection with the performance of their respective obligations under this Lease and the use and occupancy of the Premises and the Building.

**Section 10.2 --- Healthcare Regulatory Compliance.** The parties acknowledge that Tenant is a clinical reference laboratory and that Landlord is a physician group practice, and that certain financial relationships between such entities are subject to regulation under federal and state healthcare laws. The parties intend that this Lease and the rental arrangement described herein comply with all applicable healthcare laws and regulations, including without limitation the federal physician self-referral law, 42 U.S.C. § 1395nn (the \"Stark Law\"), and applicable exceptions thereto, including the rental of office space exception set forth at 42 C.F.R. § 411.357(a), and the federal Anti-Kickback Statute, 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7b(b), and applicable safe harbors thereto, including the space rental safe harbor set forth at 42 C.F.R. § 1001.952(b).

**Section 10.3 --- Fair Market Value Representation.** The parties represent and warrant that the rental rate and other terms of this Lease are consistent with fair market value, are commercially reasonable, and have been determined without regard to the volume or value of any referrals or other business generated between the parties or any physicians affiliated with Landlord and Tenant. The parties have relied upon the Lakeshore Appraisal (dated September 15, 2020, prepared by Lakeshore Valuation Group, LLC) in making this determination. Both parties have had the opportunity to consult with independent legal and financial advisors regarding the terms of this Lease.

**Section 10.4 --- No Referral Requirement.** Nothing in this Lease requires or is intended to require either party to refer patients, clients, specimens, or any business to the other party or to any entity affiliated with the other party. Each party retains complete and independent professional judgment regarding all referral decisions. Neither the execution of this Lease nor any payment hereunder is conditioned upon or related to the making of or the volume of referrals by either party.

**Section 10.5 --- CLIA Compliance.** Tenant shall at all times during the Lease Term maintain current CLIA certification and Ohio laboratory licensure for all clinical laboratory activities conducted on or from the Premises. Tenant shall promptly notify Landlord of any material change in the status of Tenant\'s CLIA certification or Ohio laboratory licensure.

**[ARTICLE XI --- ENTIRE AGREEMENT; AMENDMENTS]{.underline}**

**Section 11.1 --- Entire Agreement.** This Lease, together with all Exhibits attached hereto, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the lease of the Premises and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations, warranties, commitments, offers, contracts, and writings between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof. No prior or contemporaneous agreement, whether oral or written, shall be effective to contradict, modify, or supplement the terms of this Lease unless expressly incorporated herein.

**Section 11.2 --- Amendments.** This Lease may not be modified, amended, or supplemented except by a written instrument executed by both Landlord and Tenant. No oral modification or amendment shall be effective for any purpose.

**Section 11.3 --- No Other Agreements.** Except as expressly set forth in this Lease, neither party has made any representation, warranty, or promise to the other party, and no other agreement, arrangement, or understanding exists between the parties relating to the Premises or the transactions contemplated hereby. Each party acknowledges that it has not been induced to enter into this Lease by any representation or promise not expressly contained herein.

**[ARTICLE XII --- MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 12.1 --- Governing Law.** This Lease shall be governed by, construed in accordance with, and enforced under the laws of the State of Ohio, without regard to its conflict of laws principles.

**Section 12.2 --- Notices.** All notices, demands, consents, approvals, and other communications required or permitted under this Lease shall be in writing and shall be deemed duly given when (a) delivered personally, (b) sent by nationally recognized overnight courier service, or (c) sent by certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid, addressed as follows:

> If to Landlord:
>
> Greenfield Health Partners, LLC 2800 Riverside Medical Plaza, Suite 400 Columbus, OH 43215
>
> Attn: Alan Cromdale Consulting, Chief Financial Officer
>
> If to Tenant:
>
> Pinnacle Reference Laboratory, Inc. 2800 Riverside Medical Plaza, Suite 105 Columbus, OH 43215
>
> Attn: Sandra Cho, Chief Executive Officer

Either party may change its address for notices by providing written notice to the other party in accordance with this Section 12.2.

**Section 12.3 --- Severability.** If any provision of this Lease is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable by any court of competent jurisdiction, such holding shall not affect the validity, legality, or enforceability of the remaining provisions of this Lease, and such remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.

**Section 12.4 --- Waiver.** No waiver by either party of any breach or default of any provision of this Lease shall be deemed a waiver of any other breach or default, whether of the same or any other provision. No waiver shall be effective unless made in writing and signed by the waiving party.

**Section 12.5 --- Binding Effect.** This Lease shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties hereto and their respective heirs, executors, administrators, legal representatives, successors, and permitted assigns.

**Section 12.6 --- Counterparts.** This Lease may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Execution and delivery of this Lease by exchange of facsimile or electronic copies bearing the signatures of the parties shall constitute a valid and binding execution and delivery.

**Section 12.7 --- Captions.** The article and section captions contained in this Lease are inserted for convenience of reference only and shall not affect the meaning or interpretation of any provision of this Lease.

**Section 12.8 --- Time of Essence.** Time is of the essence with respect to all dates and time periods set forth in this Lease.

**Section 12.9 --- Authority.** Each party represents and warrants to the other that it has full power and authority to enter into and perform its obligations under this Lease, and that the execution and delivery of this Lease has been duly authorized by all necessary corporate or company action. **[UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT]{.underline}**

**[FOR THE SOUTHERN DISTRICT OF OHIO]{.underline}**

**[EASTERN DIVISION]{.underline}**

\ 

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **UNITED STATES OF AMERICA, *ex rel.* MIRANDA HALE,**                                                                                                 **Case No. 2:24-cv-04187**
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -----------------------------------
  \<!\-- indent:2 \--\>Plaintiff-Relator,\<!\-- /indent \--\>                                                                                           Judge: **\_\_\_\_\_**

  v\.                                                                                                                                                   Filed: **October 18, 2024**

  GREENFIELD HEALTH PARTNERS, LLC; BUCKEYE SURGICAL CENTER, LLC; DR. RAYMOND K. STEIN, M.D., individually; and DR. PRIYA NARAYAN, M.D., individually,   

  \<!\-- indent:2 \--\>Defendants.\<!\-- /indent \--\>                                                                                                  
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

\ 

**[COMPLAINT]{.underline}**

**(Filed Under Seal Pursuant to 31 U.S.C. § 3730(b)(2))**

\[EXCERPTS --- Selected paragraphs reproduced for internal review purposes\]

**[I. INTRODUCTORY PARAGRAPHS]{.underline}**

¶ 1. This is a *qui tam* action brought under the False Claims Act (\"FCA\"), 31 U.S.C. §§ 3729--3733, by Relator Miranda Hale on behalf of the United States of America. This action seeks to recover treble damages and civil penalties for false and fraudulent claims submitted to the Medicare and Medicaid programs by Defendants Greenfield Health Partners, LLC (\"Greenfield\"), Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC (\"Buckeye\"), Dr. Raymond K. Stein, M.D. (\"Dr. Stein\"), and Dr. Priya Narayan, M.D. (\"Dr. Narayan\") (collectively, \"Defendants\").

¶ 2. Defendants have engaged in a systematic scheme to violate the federal physician self-referral statute, commonly known as the Stark Law, 42 U.S.C. § 1395nn, by: (a) paying employed physicians per-referral bonuses to incentivize referrals of designated health services (\"DHS\") to Greenfield-affiliated entities; (b) providing below-fair-market-value lease arrangements to entities that are significant recipients of referrals from Greenfield physicians; and (c) distributing profits from an affiliated ambulatory surgery center based on individual physician referral volume rather than proportional ownership interests.

¶ 3. Claims submitted to Medicare in violation of the Stark Law are, by operation of 42 U.S.C. § 1395nn(g)(1), not payable by the federal government and constitute false claims under the FCA. In fiscal year 2023 alone, Greenfield submitted over \$100 million in claims to the Medicare program --- claims that are tainted by the systematic Stark Law violations described herein.

¶ 4. Relator Miranda Hale is a former Billing Manager of Greenfield Health Partners, LLC, employed from June 2019 through September 2024. During her more than five years of employment, Relator had direct access to Greenfield\'s billing records, physician compensation data, lease agreements, and compliance files. Relator has direct, personal knowledge of the violations alleged herein, which she acquired in the course and scope of her employment duties, including the reconciliation of physician compensation, the processing of lease payments, and the submission of Medicare claims.

\[Paragraphs 5--8 (Jurisdiction and Venue) omitted\]

**[II. THE PARTIES]{.underline}**

¶ 9. **Relator Miranda Hale** is an individual and resident of Franklin County, Ohio. Ms. Hale was employed by Greenfield Health Partners, LLC in the capacity of Billing Manager from approximately June 2019 through September 2024. Her responsibilities included overseeing Medicare and Medicaid claims submission, physician compensation reconciliation, and lease payment processing for Greenfield and its affiliated entities. Ms. Hale is an original source of the information underlying the allegations in this Complaint within the meaning of 31 U.S.C. § 3730(e)(4).

¶ 10. **Greenfield Health Partners, LLC** is an Ohio limited liability company formed on March 14, 2009, bearing EIN 31-4527893, with its principal office located at 2800 Riverside Medical Plaza, Suite 400, Columbus, OH 43215. Greenfield is a multispecialty physician group comprising 87 physicians --- 52 member-owners and 35 employed physicians --- practicing across 12 locations in the Columbus, Ohio metropolitan area. Greenfield provides designated health services including, *inter alia*, laboratory testing, diagnostic imaging, and surgical services. In 2023, Greenfield submitted approximately \$98.3 million in claims to the Medicare and Medicaid programs.

¶ 11. **Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC** is an Ohio limited liability company formed on August 22, 2016, located at 2850 Riverside Medical Plaza, Suite 100, Columbus, OH 43215. Buckeye is a Medicare-certified ambulatory surgery center (\"ASC\") owned 60% by Greenfield Health Partners, LLC, 25% by Dr. Raymond K. Stein personally, and 15% by Dr. Priya Narayan personally. In 2023, Buckeye reported annual revenue of approximately \$23.4 million, of which approximately \$16.8 million was attributable to the Medicare and Medicaid programs.

¶ 12. **Dr. Raymond K. Stein, M.D.** is an individual and board-certified orthopedic surgeon who serves as Managing Member and Chief Medical Officer of Greenfield Health Partners. Dr. Stein holds a 4.2% ownership interest in Greenfield and a 25% personal ownership interest in Buckeye Surgical Center. Dr. Stein also serves as Medical Director of Buckeye Surgical Center, for which he receives compensation of over \$200,000 annually. Dr. Stein\'s total compensation from all Greenfield and Buckeye sources exceeded \$1.2 million in 2023. As described more fully below, Dr. Stein was the architect and primary beneficiary of the unlawful compensation and referral arrangements at issue in this action.

¶ 13. **Dr. Priya Narayan, M.D.** is an individual and board-certified cardiologist who serves as a member physician of Greenfield Health Partners. Dr. Narayan holds a 3.1% ownership interest in Greenfield and a 15% personal ownership interest in Buckeye Surgical Center. Critically, Dr. Narayan serves on Greenfield\'s Compensation Committee --- the body responsible for setting physician compensation --- despite her direct personal financial interest in the referral-based compensation arrangements at issue in this Complaint.

\[Paragraphs 14--18 (Additional Parties and Agents) omitted\]

**[III. FACTUAL BACKGROUND --- GREENFIELD\'S BUSINESS AND REFERRAL RELATIONSHIPS]{.underline}**

¶ 19. Greenfield operates as a multispecialty medical group providing orthopedic, cardiology, internal medicine, radiology, general surgery, urology, and neurology services to patients throughout central Ohio. Greenfield owns and operates in-office ancillary services laboratories at 8 of its 12 locations and maintains extensive referral relationships with multiple entities to which it directs designated health services, including imaging, laboratory, and surgical services.

¶ 20. Greenfield\'s employed internal medicine physicians serve as the primary \"gateway\" for referrals within the Greenfield system. These physicians refer patients to Greenfield-affiliated specialists, the Buckeye Surgical Center, and Greenfield\'s in-house ancillary services, generating substantial Medicare and Medicaid revenue for Defendants. The internal medicine physicians are the linchpin of Greenfield\'s revenue model, and their referral patterns are critical to the financial performance of the entire Greenfield enterprise.

¶ 21. Greenfield leases office space at its Riverside Medical Plaza campus to multiple entities that are significant recipients of referrals from Greenfield physicians, including ClearView Diagnostic Imaging, LLC (\"ClearView\"), which occupies Suite 210, and Pinnacle Reference Laboratory, Inc. (\"Pinnacle\"), which occupies Suite 105. Both of these entities are substantially dependent on Greenfield physician referrals for their patient and specimen volume.

¶ 22. Relator personally processed billing and compensation data for Greenfield throughout her five-year tenure and observed first-hand that Greenfield\'s compensation and leasing practices were structured to incentivize and reward physician referrals to Greenfield-affiliated entities and DHS providers, rather than to compensate physicians for the fair market value of their personally performed services.

\[Paragraphs 23--32 (Regulatory Background --- Stark Law and FCA) omitted\]

**[IV. COUNT I: PER-REFERRAL COMPENSATION SCHEME --- VIOLATIONS OF THE STARK LAW AND THE FALSE CLAIMS ACT]{.underline}**

**A. The \"Referral Quality Bonus\" Program (¶¶ 33--40)**

¶ 33. In or about January 2022, Greenfield introduced a new physician compensation component designated as the \"Referral Quality Bonus\" through a Compensation Plan Update Memorandum dated January 10, 2022. The memorandum was authored by Dr. Raymond K. Stein, in his capacity as Managing Member, and Alan Cromdale Consulting, Greenfield\'s Chief Financial Officer.

¶ 34. Under the Referral Quality Bonus program, Greenfield pays employed physicians **\$200 for each \"qualified internal referral\"** made to a Greenfield-affiliated specialist, the Buckeye Surgical Center, or Greenfield\'s in-house ancillary services, including diagnostic imaging and laboratory testing. A \"qualified internal referral\" is defined as any referral by a Greenfield physician to a Greenfield-affiliated entity for services that are actually rendered to the referred patient. The payment is triggered solely by the making of a referral and the subsequent rendering of services by the referred-to entity.

¶ 35. The Referral Quality Bonus is a per-referral payment --- *i.e.*, a classic \"per-click\" arrangement --- that directly ties physician compensation to the volume of referrals for designated health services. Notwithstanding its misleading label as a \"quality\" bonus, there is no legitimate quality metric underlying this payment. The sole criterion for payment is that the physician made a referral to a Greenfield-affiliated entity and that the referred entity rendered services. There is no assessment of clinical appropriateness, patient outcomes, adherence to clinical guidelines, or any other indicia of quality.

¶ 36. In calendar year 2023, Greenfield paid a total of approximately \$1,260,000 in Referral Quality Bonuses across all 87 of its physicians. This extraordinary sum --- paid solely for the act of making referrals --- underscores the volume-driven nature of the program and the magnitude of the unlawful financial incentives at issue.

¶ 37. Relator personally reconciled compensation data showing the Referral Quality Bonus payments. By way of example, Dr. Thomas Wellford, an employed internal medicine physician, received \$78,000 in Referral Quality Bonuses in 2023, corresponding to approximately 520 \"qualified internal referrals\" during that year. Dr. Wellford\'s Referral Quality Bonus alone exceeded his annual productivity bonus, demonstrating the outsized role that referral-based compensation plays in Greenfield\'s physician pay structure.

¶ 38. The Referral Quality Bonus was never incorporated into individual physician employment agreements by written amendment. Dr. Wellford\'s employment agreement, executed January 15, 2022, for a two-year term expiring January 14, 2024, does not reference the Referral Quality Bonus. The bonus exists only in the separate Compensation Plan Update Memorandum, which is not appended to or incorporated by reference in any physician employment agreement. This failure to reduce the compensation arrangement to a written agreement satisfying the Stark Law\'s documentation requirements is itself an independent violation.

¶ 39. Relator is informed and believes that the Referral Quality Bonus program was implemented without obtaining a fair market value determination from any independent valuation firm. The last comprehensive physician compensation benchmarking study conducted for Greenfield was completed by Lakeshore Valuation Group, LLC in November 2019 --- more than two years before the Referral Quality Bonus program was introduced --- and that study did not contemplate or evaluate per-referral bonus structures of the type at issue.

¶ 40. Relator reported concerns about the Referral Quality Bonus to Greenfield\'s compliance hotline in or about April 2023. The compliance officer, Patricia Langford, purported to investigate but closed the matter within weeks without referring it to the Compliance Committee, engaging outside legal counsel, or conducting any independent review of the compensation structure. Ms. Langford\'s disposition was communicated to Relator in a form email stating that the matter had been \"reviewed and resolved.\"

**B. Stark Law Violations --- Per-Referral Compensation (¶¶ 41--46)**

¶ 41. The Stark Law, 42 U.S.C. § 1395nn(a), prohibits a physician from making referrals for designated health services to an entity with which the physician (or an immediate family member) has a financial relationship, unless the financial relationship fits squarely within an applicable exception. If no exception applies, the entity may not present or cause to be presented a claim to Medicare for DHS furnished pursuant to the prohibited referral.

¶ 42. The employment exception to the Stark Law, codified at 42 C.F.R. § 411.357(c), requires, among other things, that compensation paid to employed physicians: (i) is set in advance; (ii) does not exceed fair market value for services actually rendered by the employed physician; and (iii) is not determined in a manner that takes into account the volume or value of the physician\'s referrals. Each of these requirements must be satisfied independently, and failure to meet any single requirement causes the entire employment relationship to fall outside the exception.

¶ 43. The Referral Quality Bonus fails each of these requirements. First, it is calculated on a per-referral basis --- \$200 per referral --- directly and explicitly tying the physician\'s compensation to the volume of referrals for designated health services. Second, the bonus is not \"set in advance\" within the meaning of the regulation but rather varies from pay period to pay period based on the number of referrals the physician generates. Third, no fair market value analysis conducted by a qualified, independent appraiser supports the payment level or structure; the Referral Quality Bonus was introduced without any FMV determination whatsoever.

¶ 44. Because the employment exception is not satisfied, referrals made by employed physicians who receive the Referral Quality Bonus constitute prohibited referrals under the Stark Law, 42 U.S.C. § 1395nn(a)(1).

¶ 45. All claims submitted to Medicare for designated health services resulting from such prohibited referrals are not payable under 42 U.S.C. § 1395nn(g)(1), and the submission of such claims to the Medicare program constitutes false or fraudulent claims within the meaning of 31 U.S.C. § 3729(a)(1)(A) and (B).

¶ 46. Based on Relator\'s review of billing data and referral records, the estimated Medicare billings attributable to referrals generated under the Referral Quality Bonus program in calendar year 2023 exceed \$12 million.

\[Paragraphs 47--52 (Damages Calculation for Count I) omitted\]

**[V. COUNT II: BELOW-MARKET LEASE ARRANGEMENTS --- VIOLATIONS OF THE STARK LAW AND THE FALSE CLAIMS ACT]{.underline}**

**A. ClearView Diagnostic Imaging Lease (¶¶ 53--60)**

¶ 53. Greenfield Health Partners leases approximately 3,200 square feet of medical office space at 2800 Riverside Medical Plaza, Suite 210, Columbus, OH 43215, to ClearView Diagnostic Imaging, LLC (\"ClearView\"), an independently owned diagnostic imaging center. ClearView is owned by Marcus Feldstein and provides MRI, CT, ultrasound, and X-ray services.

¶ 54. The ClearView lease was executed on or about January 1, 2021, for a five-year term through December 31, 2025. The lease provides for rental payments of \$18.00 per square foot per year, or \$57,600 annually (\$4,800 per month), for the 3,200-square-foot premises.

¶ 55. An independent fair market value appraisal conducted by Lakeshore Valuation Group, LLC, dated September 15, 2020, determined that comparable medical office space at the Riverside Medical Plaza had a fair market rental value in the range of \$28.00 to \$32.00 per square foot per year. This appraisal was available to Greenfield\'s management at the time the ClearView lease was negotiated and executed.

¶ 56. The ClearView lease rate of \$18.00 per square foot is thus \$10.00 to \$14.00 per square foot per year below the appraised fair market value, representing an annual subsidy to ClearView of between \$32,000 and \$44,800. Over the five-year lease term, this below-market discount amounts to **over \$250,000** in aggregate below-market-value remuneration from Greenfield to ClearView --- a massive subsidy that is directly attributable to the referral relationship between the parties.

¶ 57. The ClearView lease contains no escalation clause, rent adjustment mechanism, or periodic market reset provision to adjust the rental rate over the five-year term. The lease rate was thus locked in at a below-market level for the entirety of a five-year period, with no mechanism to bring the rate into alignment with fair market value as market conditions evolved.

¶ 58. Relator is informed and believes, based on billing records she processed during her employment, that approximately 68% of ClearView\'s patient volume originates from referrals by Greenfield physicians. ClearView is thus substantially dependent on Greenfield referrals for its ongoing business, creating a powerful incentive structure: Greenfield provides ClearView with below-market rent, and ClearView in turn serves as a preferred referral destination for Greenfield physicians.

¶ 59. The below-market lease constitutes remuneration from Greenfield to ClearView that takes into account the volume and value of referrals between the parties. There is no legitimate, arms-length business justification for leasing prime medical office space at a rate 35% to 44% below its appraised fair market value to an entity whose business depends on Greenfield referrals.

**B. Pinnacle Reference Laboratory Lease (¶¶ 61--64)**

¶ 61. Greenfield Health Partners also leases approximately 1,800 square feet of medical office space at 2800 Riverside Medical Plaza, Suite 105, Columbus, OH 43215, to Pinnacle Reference Laboratory, Inc. (\"Pinnacle\"), an independently owned clinical reference laboratory. Pinnacle\'s Chief Executive Officer is Sandra Cho.

¶ 62. The Pinnacle lease was executed on or about March 1, 2022, for a three-year term through February 28, 2025. The lease provides for rental payments of \$22.00 per square foot per year, or \$39,600 annually (\$3,300 per month), for the 1,800-square-foot premises.

¶ 63. The Pinnacle lease rate of \$22.00 per square foot is also below the \$28.00 to \$32.00 per square foot fair market value range established by the Lakeshore Valuation Group appraisal. Notably, the Lakeshore appraisal relied upon to support the Pinnacle lease was dated September 15, 2020 --- approximately 18 months before the Pinnacle lease was executed in March 2022 --- rendering it stale and unreliable as a measure of then-current fair market value. No updated appraisal was obtained before or at the time of the Pinnacle lease execution.

¶ 64. Relator is informed and believes that approximately 55% of Pinnacle\'s specimen volume originates from referrals by Greenfield physicians, making Pinnacle, like ClearView, substantially dependent on Greenfield referrals for its operations.

**C. Stark Law Violations --- Lease Arrangements (¶¶ 65--68)**

¶ 65. The Stark Law rental of office space exception, codified at 42 C.F.R. § 411.357(a), requires, among other conditions, that: (i) the lease is set out in writing and signed by the parties; (ii) the term of the lease is at least one year; (iii) the rental charges over the term of the lease are set in advance, are consistent with fair market value, and are not determined in a manner that takes into account the volume or value of referrals or other business generated between the parties; and (iv) the lease would be commercially reasonable even if no referrals were made between the lessor and the lessee.

¶ 66. The ClearView and Pinnacle leases fail the fair market value requirement. Both lease rates are significantly below the appraised fair market value for the same space at the Riverside Medical Plaza, as established by Defendants\' own retained appraiser. The substantial discount provided to entities that are major recipients of Greenfield physician referrals creates a strong inference --- indeed, a compelling conclusion --- that the below-market rent constitutes remuneration taking into account the referral relationships between the parties. The absence of any escalation clause in the ClearView lease further evidences the parties\' intent to maintain the below-market subsidy over the full lease term.

¶ 67. Because the rental exception is not satisfied, referrals from Greenfield physicians to ClearView and Pinnacle constitute prohibited referrals under the Stark Law, and all claims submitted to Medicare for designated health services resulting from those referrals are not payable under 42 U.S.C. § 1395nn(g)(1) and constitute false claims under the FCA.

¶ 68. Relator is aware that Greenfield leases other office space at the Riverside Medical Plaza, including to Ohio Heart & Vascular Associates, LLC at market rates consistent with the Lakeshore appraisal. This fact further demonstrates that Defendants knew the applicable fair market value for space at the Riverside Medical Plaza and deliberately chose to lease to ClearView and Pinnacle at below-market rates --- a disparity that can only be explained by the referral relationships at issue.

\[Paragraphs 69--72 (Damages Calculation for Count II) omitted\]

**[VI. COUNT III: BUCKEYE SURGICAL CENTER PROFIT DISTRIBUTION SCHEME --- VIOLATIONS OF THE STARK LAW AND THE FALSE CLAIMS ACT]{.underline}**

**A. Referral-Based Profit Distribution (¶¶ 73--82)**

¶ 73. Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC is owned 60% by Greenfield Health Partners, LLC, 25% by Dr. Raymond K. Stein personally, and 15% by Dr. Priya Narayan personally. Both Dr. Stein and Dr. Narayan are member physicians of Greenfield who regularly refer patients to Buckeye for surgical procedures, including orthopedic, cardiac, urologic, and general surgical procedures, all of which constitute designated health services under the Stark Law.

¶ 74. The Buckeye Surgical Center Operating Agreement, executed on August 22, 2016, and never amended, provides at Section 7.3 that profit distributions to members shall be made \"in proportion to each member\'s surgical case referral volume to the Center, adjusted quarterly.\" This provision is explicit on its face: the financial return on each member\'s ownership interest is determined not by the member\'s proportional capital contribution or ownership percentage, but by the number of surgical cases the member (or, in the case of Greenfield, its physicians) refers to Buckeye.

¶ 75. This profit distribution formula directly ties the financial return on ownership to the volume of surgical case referrals, rather than to the member\'s proportional ownership interest. This is the very type of volume-based return on investment that the Stark Law is designed to prohibit.

¶ 76. Additionally, within Greenfield Health Partners itself, the Greenfield Operating Agreement provides for a \"referral credit\" mechanism whereby each Greenfield physician who refers a surgical case to Buckeye receives a credit equal to 0.5% of the facility fee revenue generated by that referred case. This referral credit is added to the individual physician\'s annual profit distribution from Greenfield, directly augmenting the physician\'s personal income in proportion to the volume and value of surgical referrals to Buckeye.

¶ 77. In calendar year 2023, Buckeye performed approximately 900 surgical cases, generating approximately \$7,380,000 in total facility fee revenue, based on an average facility fee of approximately \$8,200 per case. The 0.5% referral credit applied to this facility fee revenue yielded approximately \$36,900 in total referral credits distributed among individual Greenfield physicians who referred surgical cases to Buckeye during 2023.

¶ 78. Dr. Stein personally referred 342 of the 900 cases performed at Buckeye in 2023 --- approximately 38% of Buckeye\'s total surgical volume. Overall, Greenfield physicians accounted for approximately 78% of Buckeye\'s case volume (approximately 702 cases), generating approximately \$13.1 million in Medicare revenue for Buckeye. The concentration of referrals from Greenfield physicians to a Greenfield-owned surgical center underscores the self-referral nature of these arrangements.

¶ 79. The referral credit mechanism creates a direct, per-referral financial incentive for individual Greenfield physicians to refer surgical cases to Buckeye rather than to competing ambulatory surgery centers or hospital outpatient departments. Each additional referral results in a quantifiable, per-case financial benefit to the referring physician.

¶ 80. Dr. Stein, as Managing Member of Greenfield and Medical Director of Buckeye, was in a unique position to implement and personally benefit from this referral-based distribution scheme. Dr. Stein\'s total compensation from all Greenfield and Buckeye sources exceeded \$1,224,000 in 2023, including approximately \$847,000 in base salary, \$215,000 in quality bonus, and \$162,000 in profit distribution from Greenfield, in addition to his medical directorship compensation from Buckeye. Dr. Stein\'s dual roles gave him both the motive and the means to design compensation structures that maximized his personal financial return from the Greenfield-Buckeye referral relationship.

¶ 81. Dr. Narayan, as a 15% owner of Buckeye and a member of Greenfield\'s Compensation Committee, similarly benefited from and exercised authority over the referral-based compensation structure. Dr. Narayan\'s total compensation from all sources exceeded \$897,000 in 2023. Her simultaneous service on the Compensation Committee --- the body responsible for approving physician compensation arrangements --- while personally benefiting from referral-based distributions represents a fundamental conflict of interest that pervaded Greenfield\'s governance.

¶ 82. Relator became aware of the referral credit mechanism and the Buckeye profit distribution formula through her review of quarterly reconciliation reports processed by Greenfield\'s billing department. These reports, which Relator prepared and transmitted to Greenfield\'s CFO, Alan Cromdale Consulting, on a quarterly basis, reflected the referral-based distribution calculations in detail.

**B. Stark Law Violations --- Profit Distribution (¶¶ 83--88)**

¶ 83. The Stark Law\'s prohibition on self-referrals extends to indirect compensation arrangements. Under 42 C.F.R. § 411.354(c)(2), an indirect compensation arrangement exists where: (a) there is an unbroken chain of financial relationships between the referring physician and the entity furnishing DHS; (b) the referring physician receives aggregate compensation from the person or entity in the chain with which the physician has a direct financial relationship that varies with, or takes into account, the volume or value of referrals or other business generated by the referring physician for the entity furnishing DHS; and (c) the entity furnishing DHS has actual knowledge of, or acts in reckless disregard or deliberate ignorance of, the fact that the referring physician receives such aggregate compensation.

¶ 84. The referral credit mechanism creates precisely such an indirect compensation arrangement: Greenfield physicians refer surgical cases to Buckeye; Buckeye generates facility fee revenue from those referred cases; Greenfield, as a 60% owner of Buckeye, receives profit distributions from Buckeye; and Greenfield in turn a

llocates a portion of those distributions to individual physicians based on each physician\'s referral volume through the 0.5% referral credit. The compensation received by the individual referring physician thus varies directly and proportionally with the volume and value of that physician\'s referrals to Buckeye.

¶ 85. The Buckeye-level profit distribution formula --- distributing profits \"in proportion to each member\'s surgical case referral volume to the Center, adjusted quarterly\" --- independently violates the Stark Law because it conditions the financial return on an ownership or investment interest upon the volume of referrals rather than ownership percentages. Under 42 C.F.R. § 411.354(d)(4), returns on investment that are distributed in a manner that is directly related to the volume or value of referrals are treated as compensation arrangements subject to the Stark Law\'s prohibitions.

¶ 86. No applicable Stark Law exception shelters these arrangements. The group practice exception, 42 C.F.R. § 411.352, requires, among other conditions, that profit distributions from designated health services within the group not be determined in a manner that is directly related to the volume or value of the physician\'s referrals. 42 C.F.R. § 411.352(i). The referral credit mechanism, which ties individual physician distributions to the physician\'s referral volume, fails this requirement on its face.

¶ 87. All claims submitted to Medicare for surgical services performed at Buckeye Surgical Center on referrals from Greenfield physicians constitute prohibited referrals and are false or fraudulent claims under 31 U.S.C. § 3729(a)(1)(A) and (B).

¶ 88. Based on Relator\'s review of billing data and referral records, the estimated Medicare exposure from prohibited referrals to Buckeye Surgical Center in calendar year 2023 alone exceeds \$13 million.

\[Paragraphs 89--92 (Damages Calculation for Count III) omitted\]

**[VII. COMPLIANCE FAILURES AND SCIENTER ALLEGATIONS]{.underline}**

¶ 93. Defendants acted knowingly, or with reckless disregard or deliberate ignorance of the truth or falsity of the information, in submitting and causing to be submitted false claims to the Medicare program resulting from the Stark Law violations described herein. As set forth below, Defendants\' compliance infrastructure was inadequate by design, their compliance officers lacked independence, and their response to credible reports of potential violations was to dismiss those reports without meaningful investigation.

¶ 94. Greenfield maintained a compliance program that was, on information and belief, inadequate to detect, prevent, or remediate Stark Law violations. The compliance program was adopted on or about April 15, 2021, but has not been meaningfully updated or enforced since its adoption. The program\'s policies and procedures are generic and do not address the specific compensation arrangements, lease structures, or referral-based profit distributions at issue in this action.

¶ 95. The Chief Compliance Officer, Patricia Langford, was hired in April 2021 but lacks independent authority to investigate or remediate compliance concerns. Ms. Langford reports to Alan Cromdale Consulting, the CFO, rather than to an independent compliance body. The Compliance Committee is chaired by Dr. Stein --- the same individual who is the Managing Member of Greenfield, the Medical Director of Buckeye, and the primary architect and beneficiary of the unlawful compensation arrangements at issue. This structural conflict of interest renders the Compliance Committee incapable of exercising independent oversight.

¶ 96. In calendar year 2023, the compliance hotline received at least three reports raising concerns directly relevant to the violations alleged in this Complaint. First, in or about April 2023, Relator submitted a report concerning the Referral Quality Bonus and its per-referral compensation structure. Second, in or about August 2023, a separate reporter raised concerns concerning non-group radiologists billing under Greenfield\'s group NPI number. Third, in or about November 2023, a report was submitted concerning the below-market lease rates charged to ClearView and Pinnacle. All three reports were summarily closed by Ms. Langford without Compliance Committee review, without engagement of outside legal counsel, and without any discernible investigation or corrective action.

¶ 97. Greenfield conducted no compliance training for physicians or staff in 2023 or 2024, performed no compliance risk assessment at any time since the compliance program\'s initial adoption in 2021, and as of September 2024 --- the date of Relator\'s termination --- had indefinitely postponed its scheduled quarterly Compliance Committee meeting without explanation.

¶ 98. Relator personally raised concerns about the Referral Quality Bonus program and the below-market lease arrangements to her direct supervisor and, upon receiving no response, to the compliance hotline. Relator followed up on her hotline reports on multiple occasions, only to be informed that the matters had been closed. Relator\'s concerns were ignored.

¶ 99. Relator\'s employment was terminated in September 2024, approximately five months after she filed her most recent compliance hotline report concerning the ClearView lease terms and after she had begun raising pointed questions about the basis for the below-market rental rates to her supervisor and to Alan Cromdale Consulting.

\[Paragraphs 100--104 (Retaliation Allegations) omitted\]

**[VIII. PRAYER FOR RELIEF]{.underline}**

¶ 105. WHEREFORE, Relator Miranda Hale, on behalf of the United States of America, respectfully requests that this Court enter judgment against Defendants Greenfield Health Partners, LLC; Buckeye Surgical Center, LLC; Dr. Raymond K. Stein, M.D.; and Dr. Priya Narayan, M.D., jointly and severally, and award the following relief:

> ¶ 106(a). Treble damages under 31 U.S.C. § 3729(a)(1)(G) for all false claims submitted to the Medicare and Medicaid programs as a result of the Stark Law violations described herein;
>
> ¶ 106(b). Civil penalties of not less than \$11,665 and not more than \$23,331 per false claim, as adjusted for inflation, pursuant to 31 U.S.C. § 3729(a)(1);
>
> ¶ 106(c). The maximum relator\'s share of any recovery obtained pursuant to 31 U.S.C. § 3730(d), whether by judgment, settlement, or other resolution;
>
> ¶ 106(d). Reasonable attorneys\' fees, costs, and expenses incurred in bringing this action, pursuant to 31 U.S.C. § 3730(d); and
>
> ¶ 106(e). Such other and further relief as this Court deems just and proper.

¶ 107. Relator estimates that the total Medicare claims tainted by the Stark Law violations described herein exceed \$30 million for calendar year 2023 alone, encompassing the prohibited referrals generated through the Referral Quality Bonus program (Count I), the below-market lease arrangements (Count II), and the Buckeye Surgical Center referral-based profit distribution scheme (Count III). This figure does not include claims submitted in prior years during which these arrangements were in effect, nor does it account for Medicaid claims, which would increase the total exposure significantly.
